title: Name controls by the words they show, so the design-system stories pass axe 4.14
entry:
**Screen readers and voice control now hear the words a control shows.** Several controls were
named in a way that left out what was printed on them, so a person using voice control could not say
the label they saw. A folder in the file manager's tree is now named with its file count ("Pleadings
12 files"), the month heading of a small calendar starts with the month it shows ("June 2026, choose a
month"), and the Error ID chip on a failure band reads the ID and what pressing it does ("Error ID
err_7FQ2K9XW, copy").

**For builders.** The accessibility checker the design system's stories run under (axe-core 4.14,
arrived with the dependency refresh) now enforces `label-content-name-mismatch`, which it used to
treat as experimental, and 23 stories failed it or the changes beside it. Fixed per component rather
than by turning the rule off:

- `Tree`: the treeitem is now the row, and an open branch is the row's sibling `role="group"` inside
  a `role="none"` `<li>` (levels, set sizes and positions stay explicit). A treeitem that wrapped its
  children showed every descendant's label inside itself. `Tree` takes an optional `itemLabel` for a
  row whose `trailing` content shows text; `FolderTree` uses it for the file count. Drag marks land on
  the treeitem itself now.
- `MergeFieldPicker`'s trigger is a `combobox`, the role Bits 2.20 gave the `Select` trigger, so the
  field's label names it and the chosen field is its value. Story queries for both moved from
  `button` to `combobox`.
- `FolderTree` clips its loading placeholder instead of scrolling it, since a scroll region with
  nothing focusable fails `scrollable-region-focusable`.
- Two stories asserted more than they meant: the day-lanes story now expects the deposition held in
  two calendars twice, and the exchange story reads which side a turn sits on from its mark, not from
  the width of the member's question.

title: Meetings: stronger noise removal, a pure-Rust filter in an audio worklet
entry:
**Stronger noise removal in meetings, in Rust.** `crates/noise-suppression-core` wraps nnnoiseless
(the pure-Rust port of RNNoise, BSD-3, built with no default features so no C reaches the tree) and
compiles to WebAssembly for `packages/noise-suppression`. The web client runs it in an
`AudioWorklet` (`effects/noise-removal.worklet.ts`) on 480-sample frames, with the engine module
compiled on the main thread and passed in `processorOptions`, and swaps the filtered track into the
microphone's sender with `replaceTrack`. It is a second, opt-in switch beside the browser's own noise
reduction, which it asks off while it runs; a failure turns it off and hands the sound back. The web
worker's build gains the `rust-wasm-build-noise-suppression` task. Measured in Chromium against a
fake microphone: a low rumble at 0.10 RMS came out at about 0.001, and a voiced sound was kept.

title: Move the favourite star into the page menu
entry: **The favourite star moves into the page menu.** `page-actions-menu.svelte` now opens with Add to Favorites (Remove from Favorites, with the star glyph filled gold, once the page is saved), ahead of Copy Link and Open in New Tab, and `ScreenHeader` no longer draws a separate star. `favorite-control.svelte` is removed; the favourites store is unchanged, so every saved favourite carries over. `favoritable={false}` still drops the whole menu. The ruling is updated in `docs/conventions/design-corrections.md`.

title: Meetings: recording, transcripts, summaries and live captions, shipped switched off until the deployment is set up
entry:
**The meeting switches have a writer.** `meetings.recordingEnabled`, `meetings.captionsEnabled`,
`meetings.summariesEnabled` and `meetings.recordedTrackCeiling` were read by the recording start
route, the recorder and the summary consumer and written by nothing, so every firm's recording
answered `meeting-recording-not-configured` and every summary was refused `disabled`.
`GET`/`PATCH /api/v1/firm/meetings/settings` (`routes/meeting-settings.ts`,
`firmMeetingSettings.get` / `.update`) reads and writes all four: sparse, one idempotent batch with
one `firm.meeting_settings_updated` audit row, and an empty patch writes and audits nothing. The
ceiling is refused with a 422 outside 1 to `RECORDED_TRACK_CEILING_MAXIMUM` (11, the recorder's memory
arithmetic), never clamped. The read also reports two facts it never writes:
`recordingServiceConfigured`, from the same bindings check the start route's 503 reads, and
`aiProcessingEligible`, the gate a summary needs beside its own switch.

**A fourth meetings key.** `meetings:manageSettings` gates both verbs and is seeded to Owner/Admin
alone (`20261110T000108_seed-meeting-settings-permission`): recording one meeting is a practitioner's
act on `meetings:record`, deciding that every meeting may be recorded, captioned or summarized is the
firm's.

**Settings › Practice › Meetings** renders the four on the standard settings page over the shared
server-backed draft, through the generated client. The ceiling's row is composed from the read's
maximum, and a typed value outside it is refused at the Save button.

**Meeting recording, the server half: the sink and the consent mechanism.** Three per-firm tables by
one additive migration — `meeting_recording`, `meeting_recording_track` and `meeting_recording_notice`
— with every stay named by kind and by value so a guest is on the record exactly as a member is, a
nullable `breakout_id` on the recording, and a new `meetings:record` key seeded to the seats that hold
`meetings:host`. Four routes in `routes/meetings.ts`: `POST` and `DELETE /api/v1/meetings/{id}/recording`
to start and stop, `GET .../recordings` to list, and `GET .../recordings/{recordingId}/notices` for the
consent record. Stopping is the key or a live grant on the meeting, labelled `host`. Ending a meeting
stops its recording in the end's own batch. `MeetingSummary` gains `recordingState`,
`recordingConfigured` and `captionsAvailable`.

**The announcement is the consent mechanism, with a record.** The room broadcasts a `recording` frame
to every welcomed socket, guests included and never the lobby, the instant a start or stop commits; a
socket welcomed while a recording runs is told on its welcome; and the room writes a notice row for
every stay it told, one batch per fan-out with one audit row carrying the count. The room is told
before any audio is captured.

**The sink.** A `MeetingRecorder` Durable Object per recording receives each audio track from the media
routing service's WebSocket adapter, decodes the envelope with a hand-written reader, folds it to mono,
writes silence for frames that never arrived, and stages it in the firm's own bucket in uniform 8 MiB
parts. It reconciles against the room every few seconds — admitting late tracks, refusing past the
firm's track ceiling with a `lost` row, closing tracks of people who left — and stops itself when every
track is lost. The routing service dials `/internal/meeting-audio/<token>`, outside the chokepoint,
on a signed per-track token, refusing any request that carries an Origin. Recording stays off — the
start route answers 503 `meeting-recording-not-configured` — until a firm switches it on and the
deployment holds `MEETING_SINK_SIGNING_KEY`, which waits on proving the routing service keeps the sink
address intact. Composing and filing the recording are the next slice.

**Live captions, server half.** A host turns captions on for the room with a `captions` frame
(refused `captions-unavailable` where the firm's `meetings.captionsEnabled` is off or the deployment
cannot route meeting audio, `not-host` to anybody not running the meeting), and the room state carries
`captions: { by, at }` to every socket and every welcome, absent while off. A new Durable Object,
`MeetingCaptioner` (one per meeting, binding `MEETING_CAPTIONER`, migration tag
`v12-meeting-captioner`), opens a caption session for somebody only while the room's `speaking`
presence says they are talking — a routing-service adapter on their microphone dialling back through
the existing sink address on a caption token of its own `typ`, and a stream to `@cf/deepgram/nova-3`
through the new `InferencePort.openCaptionStream` (the catalog's `captioning` slot, platform-fixed,
off the firm roster; `websocket: true` on the AI binding) — and closes it three seconds after they
stop. No recording is needed. Interim and final words reach every welcomed socket as `caption` frames
naming the speaker (a guest's copy carries no firm identifier), interims coalesced to one per speaker
per half second inside a room-wide budget of ten a second, finals never held. Nothing a caption says is
stored anywhere. A caption model that fails mid-meeting closes that speaker's session and touches the
recording not at all. The AI-processing eligibility is not asked, as for the transcript of record — an
owner decision assumed and recorded in the recording design (A86). Captions are configured exactly
when recording is, so they wait on the same sink experiment and signing key. The caption strip is the
web half.

**Meeting summaries: the server half is corrected after its review.** Amendments A68 to A80 in the
recording spec.

- A task made from an action item can be deleted again: the task delete clears the item's link in its own
  batch (`clearActionItemTaskStatement`, from `@magna-carta/meetings`), and the item reads as untasked.
- A retried `POST` with the same Idempotency-Key now answers the documented body — the summary as it
  stands, or `{ taskId, actionItem }` — instead of the stored pointer.
- A summary needs the firm's AI-processing eligibility as well as `meetings.summariesEnabled`, on every
  model. The platform's own model is now `@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b` (Apache-2.0, text-only) in a catalog
  role no firm can select for the assistant, and every model hosted on Cloudflare is sent a default
  answer length when a caller names none.
- A due date is kept only when the words somebody said name its day and month one way — never a line's
  timestamp, never "the 14th" alone, never "3/12" — and a year that fits.
- The context bound reckons non-Latin text and timestamps honestly, each call has room for a reasoning
  model's answer, a long transcript's action items are kept whole rather than re-listed by a model, the
  wall clock is checked before each call, every call is metered as it completes, a call the model will
  never take stops being retried, a host's re-run no longer doubles a scheduled retry, the gate is read
  before every call, a withheld transcript is never sent, the answer is asked for in JSON mode, and a
  task's title is cut between characters. Migration
  `20261110T000107_meeting-summary-retry-and-failed-call` adds `model_failure_call` and `retry_at`.

**Meeting transcripts: an outage is outlasted, the read follows the filed document, and the words are
kept out of every log by a scan.** From the adversarial review of the transcript's server half.

- A speech model that refuses for now no longer fails a transcript after about thirty seconds: each
  refusal is counted on the row (`meeting_transcript.model_failures`, reset by progress) and the window
  is sent again after a delay doubling from thirty seconds to fifteen minutes, ten in a row before it
  fails (`apps/api-worker/src/meetings/transcript-consumer.ts`). A failure a retry could get past — the
  model, or the sweep's stall — keeps the per-speaker staged audio for the seven-day retention a failed
  compose's has; only a refusal no retry can change releases it at once.
- `GET /api/v1/meetings/{meetingId}/recordings/{recordingId}/transcript` serves lines only while the
  transcript's filed WebVTT version exists, is not trashed and is not held by the scan, and answers
  `linesWithheld` (`removed`, `held`, `unavailable`) otherwise; it is now audited, one
  `meetings.transcript.read` row of identifiers per page of lines.
- Failures are guarded on the upload session they read and, for the sweep, on what it judged stalled; a
  redelivery that meets a live lease is retried when it runs out; a lost speaker whose audio is missing
  is said not to have been heard from their first frame; a track whose staging vanishes part-way is
  refused; ingest hand-ons are best effort after the filing.
- The model's answer: a segment past the piece it was sent is dropped; the language is taken from the
  first piece of eight seconds or more and sent as the hint after; audio sent is counted in
  milliseconds (`transcribed_milliseconds`, migration
  `20261110T000105_meeting-transcript-model-failures-and-milliseconds`). The recorder's own digital
  silence no longer drags the noise floor down, and the WebVTT document strips bidirectional and
  invisible characters with the filed audio name's own set.
- `packages/meetings/test/no-transcript-text-escape.test.ts` is the repo-wide fitness scan keeping
  transcript text, speaker names and the model's prompt out of loggers, audit builders and errors.
  Amendments A45 to A56 in the recording spec.

**Meeting recording, the server half of the transcript.** Every filed recording now has a transcript,
begun in the batch that files the audio (`meeting_transcript` and `meeting_transcript_segment`, migration
`20261110T000104_meeting-transcript`) and made on the existing `meeting-recording-compose` queue as a
second kind of message, so a deployment needs no new queue. The transcript reads each track's own staged
audio — the compose no longer deletes the staging when it files — finds where its speaker was talking
from the audio's energy against the track's own noise floor (`packages/meetings/src/speech-spans.ts`),
cuts each span at thirty seconds at a pause where there is one, downsamples to 16 kHz behind an
anti-alias filter (`resample.ts`) and sends each piece to the platform's speech model with the tail of
the previous piece's words as its prompt. A window is a bounded number of model calls, claimed on the
row so two deliveries never send the same audio twice. Lines are attributed to the track they came from
— a guest's to the guest's stay — merged into reading order, and a gap line says where a speaker was
lost, refused at the ceiling, or missing. The finished transcript is filed beside the audio on the same
matter as `Meeting transcript — <event title> — <start in the event's zone>.vtt` through the upload
pipeline, with each speaker's name in every cue. The staged tracks are released when the transcript
settles, ready or failed; a model that will not answer fails it with an Error ID after three deliveries,
and the recording sweep hands a stalled transcript on and fails it after three attempts so the staging
is still released. New read: `GET /api/v1/meetings/{meetingId}/recordings/{recordingId}/transcript`
(the header and cursor-paged lines), and each recording-list entry carries `transcript`.

**Meeting recording, the server half of compose and file.** A stopped recording's staged tracks are
mixed into one mono 48 kHz WAV by a queue consumer on the new `meeting-recording-compose` queue
(`apps/api-worker/src/meetings/recording-compose-consumer.ts`): ten one-minute parts per message, each
track at its first frame's offset, summed in 32 bits and clamped once (`packages/meetings/src/pcm-mix.ts`),
the 44-byte header at the head of the first part (`packages/meetings/src/wav.ts`), about 40 MB of working
memory per invocation whatever the length or track count. The cursor is five added columns on
`meeting_recording` (migration `20261110T000102_meeting-recording-compose-cursor`). The finished recording
is filed through the upload pipeline unchanged — `initiateUpload` on the recording's matter,
`completeUploadSession`, the ingest queue — named `Meeting recording — <event title> — <start in the
event's zone>.wav`; the recording moves to `filed` with its file and version, and the staged tracks are
deleted. A sweep on the ten-minute cron (`recording-sweep.ts`) abandons a recording whose recorder has
stopped reconciling (the recorder's new `heartbeat` and `abandon`), hands a stalled compose on and fails
it with an Error ID after three attempts, and releases staged audio after seven days for a failed or
abandoned recording. `MeetingRecordingSummary` gains `failureErrorId`, and `stoppedBy` is emitted as the
actor or null. Also from the first slice: the track ceiling counts participants rather than tracks, a
guest's announcement no longer carries the recording's handle, a recording is announced once however
many requests carry its start, and ending or cancelling a meeting whose recording stopped at the same
moment no longer answers a server error.

**Meeting summaries: a ready transcript is summarized, with its action items, and an item can become a
task.** The server half; the summary card is the web half and is next.

- Every transcript that becomes ready begins a summary in the same batch (`meeting_summary`,
  `meeting_summary_action_item`, migration `20261110T000106_meeting-summary`), written on the recording's
  own queue as a third kind of message by `apps/api-worker/src/meetings/summary-consumer.ts` — no new
  queue. It is `refused` with a reason when the firm has not switched `meetings.summariesEnabled` on
  (`disabled`), when the firm has not allowed its content to reach a model at all (`not-eligible`), or
  when nobody was heard (`transcript-empty`). A firm that chose no model is summarized by the platform's
  own reasoning model hosted on Cloudflare (`@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b`), so the conversation does not
  leave the platform unless the firm chose a model that sends it elsewhere.
- The transcript is sent through `InferencePort.generateConversation` — never as an assistant
  conversation — with a platform-authored instruction (`packages/meetings/src/summary-prompt.ts`) and one
  member message of `HH:MM:SS Name: text` lines. A transcript too long for the model's context window is
  summarized a part at a time (at most five, inside one message's wall-clock budget) and combined. Every
  call's provider usage is written to the firm's token meter, including a run that did not finish.
- The answer must be one documented JSON structure; anything else fails the summary with an Error ID
  (`summary-parse.ts`). An action item's owner is linked only on an exact match to a member's name as the
  transcript knows them, and a due date only where the model quoted transcript words stating it.
- `GET` and `POST /api/v1/meetings/{meetingId}/recordings/{recordingId}/summary` read (audited, one
  `meetings.summary.read` row of identifiers) and re-run a summary; its words are withheld whenever the
  transcript's filed document is trashed, held or gone. `POST …/summary/action-items/{actionItemId}/task`
  makes an item a task through `createMatterTask`, once. The recording list entry carries `summary`.
- The inference catalog records each reasoning model's context window (and answer limit where the
  provider publishes one), and a conversation may ask for an answer length; a model hosted on Cloudflare
  takes the platform's instruction as its first `system` message. The repo-wide scan in
  `packages/meetings/test/no-transcript-text-escape.test.ts` now covers summary text too. Amendments A57
  onward in the recording spec.

**Meeting recording, the summary's web half.** The Recordings panel gains a Summary column
(`recordingSummaryText` and `recordingSummaryOpens` in
`apps/web/src/lib/meetings/screen/recording-list.ts`): "Being Written", "Read", "Could Not Be
Written" or "Not Written". Pressing it opens the new summary panel
(`apps/web/src/lib/meetings/screen/summary-panel.svelte`, its words in `summary-panel.ts`), a reading
`ActionDialog` over the list on the transcript's precedent, read through
`meetingsRecordingSummaryOptions`. The text stands under one quiet line saying it is the platform's
characterization of the conversation and not a record of it; the action items are a numbered list,
each with its owner or "No owner" and its due date through the design system's civil-date formatter.
A summary being written, one that could not be written (with its Error ID), one refused for each of
its three reasons, and a ready one whose words are withheld (in the transcript panel's words) are the
design system's `EmptyState`, decided by one pure function (`summaryBody`); a summary being written
is read again every fifteen seconds while the panel is open, and the list is read again when it
settles. **Create Task** makes nothing on its own press: it opens a `New Task` confirmation naming
who the task will be assigned to, with a box to take the owner's name off (refused, with the reason,
where the member holds neither the item nor the key to assign), and only its commit calls the task
route with a fresh idempotency key; the made task links to `/matters/{matterId}/tasks?entry={taskId}`
(`taskAddress` in `meetings-api.ts`), a task somebody else made first is said on the row and linked,
and any other refusal stands in the confirmation. **Re-run** is offered only where the session holds
`meetings:host`, behind a destructive confirmation saying the text and action items are replaced and
tasks already made are kept. Summary and action-item text is drawn and nowhere else: not logged, not
in an address, not in a failure report. Tests: `apps/web/test/meeting-summary.test.ts` and the
Summary column in `meeting-recording-list.test.ts`.

**Meeting recording, the transcript's web half.** The Recordings panel gains a Transcript column
(`recordingTranscriptText` and `recordingTranscriptOpens` in
`apps/web/src/lib/meetings/screen/recording-list.ts`): "Being Made", "Read", or "Could Not Be Made"
with the Error ID wherever the row carries one. Pressing it opens the new transcript panel
(`apps/web/src/lib/meetings/screen/transcript-panel.svelte`, its words in `transcript-panel.ts`), a
reading `ActionDialog` over the list on the precedent of who was told, so it serves the room and the
Meetings page alike. The lines are a `Conversation` read through
`meetingsRecordingTranscriptInfiniteOptions` under `paged`, two hundred at a time with Load More on
the ordinal cursor: each under its speaker (a guest marked as one), at its place in the recording as
`mm:ss` or `h:mm:ss`, and each gap as a failed turn whose warning note says whose audio is missing
and for how long, or that nothing was heard. A transcript being made, one that could not be made, and
a ready one whose lines the read withholds (`linesWithheld`: removed, held or unavailable) are the
design system's `EmptyState`, decided by one pure function (`transcriptBody`), the failure stating
its Error ID; a ready one with no lines
says "No Results" inside its frame; a read that failed is the failure notice with Retry. A
transcript being made is read again every fifteen seconds while the panel is open, and the list is
read again the moment it settles. The WebVTT document opens beside the reader through the file's
own route and `opensBeside("file")`. Line text is drawn and nowhere else: not logged, not in an
address, not in a failure report, and the region is not a live region. Tests:
`apps/web/test/meeting-transcript.test.ts` and the Transcript column in
`meeting-recording-list.test.ts`.

**Meeting recording, hardened after review of compose and file.** Each track's staged audio is a list
of stretches anchored to the instant each began (`meeting_recording_track.segments`), so a participant
whose connection drops and returns is placed where they were heard rather than up to a padded part late;
the 300-second clamp on wall-clock silence is gone. A compose consumer claims each window on the row
(`meeting_recording.compose_claimed_at`, migration
`20261110T000103_meeting-recording-segments-and-compose-claim`) so two deliveries cannot upload the same
parts; recorded progress resets the attempt count, stalls are measured from the latest stop, claim or
progress, and the record is re-read before the composite is completed. A failed compose aborts its
upload session and multipart upload in the same failure, and `initiateUpload` gets a two-day
expiry as a backstop. An abandoned recording completes its staged uploads instead of aborting them, so
the seven-day retention keeps real audio. The compose checks its layout against the declared size,
composes without a staged object missing at the start and records an Error ID for it, and cleans
hostile event titles out of the file name. Ingest's in-memory inspection ceiling is 40 MiB
(`IN_MEMORY_INSPECTION_CEILING_BYTES`), so a long recording commits through the streaming path,
hashed and size-checked and marked unscanned as oversize, rather than running out of memory. Bucket
lifecycle rules for `meeting-recordings/` and abandoned multipart uploads under `files/` are set by
provisioning. The room keeps recently stopped recordings so a late start lights nothing and starts no
recorder; a calendar cancel's last retry settles; the recording list carries the filed version's
document state, and Open appears only for the clean current version. The compose queue runs ten
consumers. Clearing a full page of staging keys stays under SQLite's bound-variable limit.

**An anonymous poll's answer leaves nothing in the idempotency record the choice could be read back
out of.** The answer route's fingerprint was an unsalted SHA-256 of the path and `{ optionIds }`, so
a choice among at most ten options was recovered by hashing each candidate, and its stored response
was the tally just before the answer, so consecutive bodies differed by exactly one choice. The route
now stores the poll's handle alone and re-reads the poll on a retry, and the chokepoint gained an
opt-in `idempotencyFingerprint: "path"` mode on `RouteMeta` (`chokepoint/idempotency-port.ts`) that
fingerprints the method and path without the body and leaves the replay decision to the handler's
`runIdempotentEffect`. The trade: a retry under the same key with different choices is answered as
the first was rather than refused 422; it can never become a second answer.

**The room's tallies cannot move backwards across a flush.** A poll's tallies are ordered by
`respondents`, which only grows; a question's by the read instant. Each flush of the per-second
bucket leaves a per-subject high-water mark under a `tally-marks` storage key, written in the same
storage turn that clears the bucket, and a poll's close raises its mark to the final count
(`room/room-coalescing.ts`, `room/room-polls.ts`).

**A reconnect while a media session is being opened no longer strands the browser.**
`admitParticipant` gives up an opening the routing service has answered, inside the gate that resets
the record, and closes its session (`abandonAnsweredOpening`, `closeUnrecordedSession` in
`room/room-media.ts`); an unanswered one is still inherited. `releaseParticipant` closes an
unrecorded session even when no roster entry was left to remove.

**The question queue.** An upvote on a question that has been taken back is refused 409 `conflict`
(withdrawal still allowed). `since` without `sinceId` is inclusive (`asked_at >= ?`), so a question
committed in the same millisecond as the last one held is no longer skipped; callers drop ids they
hold. A withdrawal's audit row names the stay the upvote was cast from. Upvote and withdrawal spend a
new member-scoped bucket, `meeting-question-upvote` (thirty a minute, keyed `member:<firm>:<user>`
through `MEMBER_SCOPED_BUCKETS`), instead of the firm's default budget.

**Meeting recording ships switched off until the deployment is set up for it.** Recording,
transcripts, summaries and live captions are now on `main`, but the recording queue
(`MEETING_RECORDING_COMPOSE`) is left unbound in `apps/api-worker/wrangler.jsonc`, because a deploy
that binds a queue the account does not have fails. The start route now also requires that queue
before it offers recording. The owner's steps are in the operations runbook under "Turning meeting
recording on".

title: Record Communication is built around the phone number, holds several calls at once, and records what happened on the line
entry:
**A recorded call says what happened on the line, and a message taken on it becomes a task.** Four nullable columns on `communication` (`caller_id_name`, `outcome`, `spam_kind`, `message_task_id`), validated in `packages/communications/src/validation.ts` (`normalizeCallOutcome`, `normalizeCallerIdName`) rather than by CHECKs, since the table is populated. Outcomes are per direction (`INBOUND_CALL_OUTCOMES`, `OUTBOUND_CALL_OUTCOMES`); a spam outcome sets the `spam` disposition and refuses a matter; a transfer needs `memberUserId`; spam, no answer and a voicemail need no notes. `POST /api/v1/communications` takes `callerIdName`, `outcome`, `spamKind` and `message`; a message is written through `createMatterTask` in the same batch as the call (a `MessageTaskWriter` handed to `logCommunication`), needs `tasks:write` and, for somebody else, `tasks:assign`, and raises the ordinary task-assignment notification. The form's Activity section is `communication-activity.svelte`; the Identification tab counts earlier spam marks on the number from the rows themselves (`number-history.ts`).

**The Record Communication window is built around the phone number, and holds several calls at once.** `communication-fields.svelte` now leads with Call / Text and Incoming / Outgoing as a pressed button group (`$lib/components/button-choice.svelte`), then `PhoneNumberField`, then the notes, then a one-line When that opens on Change; the Contact field leaves the form while a record is being made. The window (`communication-record-window.svelte`) holds a list of `CallEntry` drafts down the left of the pane, each the draft on screen rather than a copy; saving one retires it and the window closes on the last, and `recordThenIntake` no longer closes the window, so the messaging page stopped closing it too. While creating, the context tabs are Identification (`communication-identification.svelte`: the contact, their open matters read through `readDirectoryEntityMatterParties` with a search past five, and File Here) and History (`communication-number-history.svelte`: the log's own search, narrowed to rows on the same stored number). Start An Intake moved into the header menu; the subtitle is the previewed number alone, in italics. The contact choice moved to `communication-contact.ts` so the form and the panel share it.

title: Legal citations: a citation engine, a Formatted Citation component, and the Legal Citations tool
entry:
**Legal citations.** `@magna-carta/citations` is a pure engine that reads a pasted link (govinfo,
Cornell LII, eCFR, Nevada and California code pages, CourtListener) or a rough citation into fields,
keeps each field's provenance so typed values override what was read, and formats the full, short
and Id. forms in a court format (Uniform System from The Indigo Book; Nevada state courts; the
California Style Manual). The design system gains `FormattedCitation`, and `/legal-citations` is a
new top-level tool gated by `tools:legalCitations`, seeded onto the five default roles.

title: Redesign the conflicts check: parties-only panel, Report and Runs tabs, result cards, cancel
entry: **The conflicts check is redesigned, and a run can be cancelled.** The New Check panel asks for parties only and lists five locations, each a dropdown of what it searches; Firm Employees runs without a matter by looking for members among the entities a check reached (`findMemberEntities`). The check page gains Report and Runs tabs, collapsible Details, Status and Results sections, a per-location status log, result cards with filters and a review dropdown, and icon-only print and download buttons. `POST /api/v1/conflicts/checks/{checkId}/runs/{runId}/cancel` stops a run; a run summary reports `cancelled`, `cancelledByUserId` and `askedScope`. Reports say "0 results." and count results rather than candidates.

title: About Magna Carta opens a two-column About window
entry: **About Magna Carta opens a window.** The profile menu's Websites > About Magna Carta entry, previously disabled as Soon, and its command-palette twin now open an About window (`apps/web/src/lib/about/about-window.svelte`), mounted once in the app shell. The left column states the build's commit (linked to the source), release date, the signed-in member and firm from the cached session read, the build environment and the browser, with Copy Version Details putting the same lines on the clipboard (`aboutFacts`/`aboutDetailsText` in `about-facts.ts`). The right column links to the Changelog, Settings > Versions, the status page and Report an Issue; Documentation, Terms of Service, Privacy Policy and open-source licenses render as Soon. The ecosystem-site registry gains `opensWindow`, an in-application window that stands in for a site with no address yet, beside `route`.

title: Meetings: blur and image backgrounds, drawn by the product in a Worker
entry: **Background blur and image backgrounds in meetings, drawn by the product in any browser with WebGL 2 in a Worker.** `apps/web/src/lib/meetings/effects/background-effects.worker.ts` loads `@magna-carta/segmentation`, segments each camera frame at 256 by 144, steadies the mask across frames, and composites a mask-weighted blur (no halo of the person spread into the room) or a cover-fitted picture in WebGL 2. Frames reach it as `MediaStreamTrackProcessor`/`MediaStreamTrackGenerator` streams where the browser has them (nothing on the main thread), and as one `ImageBitmap` per frame through a hidden video element elsewhere (`effects/background-processor.ts`). `client/background-effects.ts` wraps the pass-through stage: the camera's own track is published until an effect is chosen, and the treated one is swapped in and out with `RTCRtpSender.replaceTrack` through the new `EffectedCapture.onChange`, so no offer is renegotiated and a member with no effect pays nothing. A treatment that cannot start or stops mid-meeting falls back to the camera with the reason in the panel. The chosen picture is cut down to 1920 by 1080 and kept in IndexedDB (`effects/background-image-store.ts`), never uploaded. The Effects popover offers None, Blur and Image. `rust-wasm-build-segmentation` joins the deploy composite and the interface Worker's build. Checked in headless Chromium with a fake camera playing a portrait, on both frame routes.

title: Name the town and the time there for a typed-in number
entry: **Caller lookup names the town and the time there.** The free answer of `communications.callerLookup` now carries, beside the area code's region, `place` (the town the number's exchange was assigned to, from libphonenumber's exchange-level geocoding rows) and `timeZone` (the IANA zone of the number's prefix, from libphonenumber's time zone map; null where the prefix spans several). Both tables are generated by `packages/caller-lookup/scripts/refresh-places.mjs`. The record screen shows "702 · Henderson, Nevada number" and "3:19 PM PST there".

title: Notifications group by day, category, priority, matter or read state
entry:
**The notification centre groups its rows.** `apps/web/src/routes/(app)/notifications` passes the
grid a `grouping` from `notification-grouping.ts` and offers `DataTable.GroupByMenu`: Day (the
default, the reader's own calendar days, ordered with the sort direction), Category, Priority,
Matter, Read State, or No Grouping. Opened, the dismissed shelf is always the last band.

title: Lay the Magnus transcript out as an exchange, and add the SourceQuote citation card
entry:
**The Magnus transcript is laid out as an exchange.** The design-system Conversation component gains
a second arrangement (`arrangement="exchange"` on `Conversation.Transcript`, with new `TurnMark`,
`TurnContent` and `TurnActions` parts); the default `record` arrangement and the meetings chat are
unchanged. `magnus-transcript.svelte` uses it: member turns on the right under the conversation
creator's real name and initials (the session read for the signed-in member, the firm roster for
anyone else), Magnus on the left behind the blackletter M, a time on every turn and a Copy control.
The conversation head names the matter it is kept on beneath the title, with its number, read
through `matter-citations.svelte.ts`. First piece of the owner's round two in
`docs/conventions/magnus-rulings.md`.

**`SourceQuote`, the citation card.** A design-system component (`@magna-carta/design-system/source-quote`)
for a quoted passage and its source: a coloured tab naming the kind (`statute` in the accent gilt,
`case` in the information blue, `file` neutral) and its number in the answer's source list, the
source's name and location with the caller's acts beside them, the passage in the display serif
inside drawn quotation marks, and a footer strip with the check it passed and where and when it was
read. It is the owner's chosen citation style for Magnus (`docs/conventions/magnus-rulings.md`,
R2.8). Magnus answers do not use it yet: an answer is plain text today, and it needs source-structured
answers first. Also spells the exchange arrangement's speaker tracking with the `--mc-tracking-normal`
token.

title: Fix four checks that are red on main: the sidebar fold in the icon rail, the caller-lookup contract, and two matter-close tests
entry:
**The caller-lookup contract passes the API conformance checks again.** The free lookup is recorded as a read-shaped POST, and the money-namespace idempotency rule now skips the POSTs that write nothing. The kept caller ID is one component shape across both routes. The two matter-close test files now send a JSON content type only when a body is sent, as the web client does.

**`Sidebar.MenuTrigger` folds in the icon rail again.** In the collapsed rail it renders inside a tooltip trigger, and the tooltip's props were spread after the caller's `onclick`, replacing it; the fold's handler now runs last, after the tooltip's. The sidebar story's truncation step moved to the labelled rail, where marks show.

title: Widen New Person's form beside the duplicate check
entry: **New Person's form is wider beside the duplicate check.** A primary pane that carries a section rail now stops at the new `size.record-form` token (832px: the record's 640px measure plus the rail) instead of `size.record-pane`, through `.mc-modal-frame-pane:has([data-record-rail])` in `modal-frame.css`. `record-sections.svelte` marks its rail. A three-field name row and the email row's kind, address and use now fit on one line.

title: Give a directory record a picture
entry: **A directory record carries a picture.** A new per-firm table, `directory_entity_photo`, holds one picture per person or organization; the bytes live in the firm's bucket under `directory-photo/<entity>/<sha256>.<ext>`, written before the row and swept after a replacement. `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /api/v1/directory/entities/{id}/photo` and `GET .../photo/content` follow the staff-photo route (PNG or JPEG only, idempotent writes, audited as `directory.entity.photo_changed` and `directory.entity.photo_removed`). The browser crops to a 512-pixel square JPEG before upload (`photo-crop.ts`, `photo-crop-dialog.svelte`), the record window shows it through `ActionDialog`'s new `leading` snippet, New Person can add one before saving, and the contact card embeds it as `PHOTO`.

title: Api-worker tests that never reach workerd run in plain Node; test workers and the tsc heap get explicit ceilings
entry: **The api-worker tests that never reach the Workers runtime now run in plain Node, and test and type-check memory have explicit ceilings.** A test file that declares `// @node-runtime` in its header runs in a second project, `apps/api-worker/vitest.node.config.ts`, with no workerd VM and no whole-app preload. That preload cost about 25 s of setup per file and most of the suite's 6.4 GB peak. The first 67 files to opt in run together in about 8 s. The other test projects share a ceiling of eight workers (`MC_TEST_MAX_WORKERS`) instead of one per CPU, and `tsc -b` runs with a 4 GB heap instead of Node's default, which is sized from system memory. On a 15 GB machine that default is 2,096 MB, against a measured peak of 1,943 MB. Measurements and reasoning: `docs/conventions/build-performance.md`, under "Test memory".

title: Look up who is calling from a typed-in number
entry: **Caller lookup on a typed number.** A whole number in the call record's number field is answered by `POST /api/v1/communications/caller-lookup` (`communications.callerLookup`): the Directory records listing it (`packages/directory/src/phone-match.ts`, matching numbers stored with or without their country code), the area code's region (`packages/caller-lookup/src/area-code.ts`, from libphonenumber's geocoding rows), and any caller ID already kept. `POST /api/v1/communications/caller-lookup/caller-identity` (`communications.callerIdentity`, idempotency required) asks Telnyx Number Lookup for the caller name and carrier through the new `@magna-carta/caller-lookup` port and keeps the answer in the new per-firm `caller_identity` table, so a number is paid for once per firm; a refused query keeps nothing. Both are gated on `communications:log` and are POSTs because the number is a client's. The paid half is dormant until `TELNYX_API_KEY` is set (runbook in `docs/conventions/operations.md`), counted as `communications.caller_lookup`. The web logic is `apps/web/src/lib/communications/caller-lookup.ts`, drawn by `caller-lookup.svelte` under the number field.

title: Meetings: end-to-end encryption design over MLS, and a pure-Rust person segmentation engine for background blur
entry:
**End-to-end encrypted meetings are designed.** `docs/specs/2026-11-09-meetings-end-to-end-encryption-design.md` uses MLS for group keys, so an encrypted meeting keeps the room's 300 participants, and SFrame per frame. Cloud recording, live captions and dial-in each pause encryption under a banner everyone sees, and encryption resumes with fresh keys afterwards. It compares the result with Zoom's and Google Meet's encrypted modes. Four experiments run before any code. The `meetings.end-to-end-encryption` ledger node moves to `designed`, on by default with the host able to switch it off at Start.

**The person-segmentation engine for background blur and image backgrounds.** `crates/segmentation-core` runs MediaPipe's landscape selfie segmenter on the pure-Rust `rten` runtime. The model was converted once to ONNX by `model/convert-tflite-to-onnx.py`, because its custom final layer defeats off-the-shelf converters, and is compiled into the WebAssembly module. `packages/segmentation` is the TypeScript seam (`ensureReady`, `loadPersonSegmenter`). Both the native test and the WebAssembly test hold the mask to the one Google's reference interpreter produces for a real portrait, on every pixel. The crate builds with SIMD128 (crate-local `.cargo/config.toml`) and at `opt-level 3` with the `rten` crates. It measures 14 ms a frame at p50 in headless Chromium and 1.16 MB gzipped. `rten` was chosen over `tract` because `tract` assembles native kernels with `cc`, which golden rule 14 would need consent for. Wired into bootstrap, the dev build and its own Docker task. It is not yet in the deploy composite, because nothing deployed imports it until the meeting client's effects Worker does.

title: Seven finished streams leave the active-work registry
Download a directory record as a PDF or plain text
entry: **A directory record downloads as a PDF or plain text, beside the contact card.** The entity window's More menu now has a Download submenu (PDF, Plain Text, Contact Card). `record-printout.ts` reads every page of the record's names, contact points, relationships and matters and lays them out as a `TabularExportDocument`, so the PDF comes from the reports' server renderer (`renderRemoteExport`, which needs `reports:export`) and the text from `renderTextExport`. Sealed identifiers are never printed.

title: The one table can group its rows into bands
entry:
**The one table can group its rows into bands.** `createDataTableGrid` takes a `grouping` thunk
(`GridGrouping`: `keyOf`, an optional `labelOf`, and an optional `order(keys, direction)` that may
flip with the sort), and `DataTable.Grid` renders a heading row per band with its count, sticky
beneath the measured header, plus an optional `bandDetail` snippet. Rows are sorted before they are
split, pinned rows stay above every band, and `rowsInView` follows the drawn order so keyboard and
range selection walk the rows as the reader sees them. `DataTable.GroupByMenu` is the matching
trigger and radio menu. The pure split is `bandedGridRows` in
`packages/design-system/src/lib/components/data-table/grid-rows.ts`; the Tasks and Notifications
screens are its first consumers.

title: Conflicts checks name who ran them and who they searched
entry: **A conflicts check names who ran it and who it searched.** The report's opening statement names the acting member from the roster (`readMemberDisplayName`) instead of quoting their handle, and reads "as a preliminary check" rather than "trigger preliminary". Each run summary and each row of the firm's log carries `subjectParties`, named from one set-valued Directory read; the check page lists them under Parties and the log gains a Parties column. A check filed on no matter reads No Matter.

title: Numbering: separators, unpadded counters, a drag-ordered editor, and numbers that sort as read
entry: **Client and matter numbering: separators, unpadded counts, and an editor that drags.** `NumberSegment`'s `date_opened` and `client_name` take an optional `separator` (`-`, `.`, `_`, `~` or empty; a slash is refused because a number is URL-safe), mirrored in the OpenAPI `NumberSegment` schema and the generated client. Absent renders as before (`20261111`, `AshcombeMercantile`), so no saved scheme changes shape; a client name's words are now folded one at a time and joined by the separator, dropping a word that folds to nothing. In `numbering-scheme-editor.svelte`, Preview sits under Current with no descriptive line under either (Current keeps its line only when nothing is in force), parts move by a grip on `DragReorderController` with Alt+Arrow as the keyboard path, the move buttons and the examples (`NUMBERING_STARTERS`) are gone, "Digits" is "Format" (counter minimum digits, year digits, separators), "Restarts the Count" is "Separate Count", the Part picker shows each kind's sample value, and a new counter starts at one digit. `compareGridRows` orders text with a numeric `Intl.Collator`, so every `DataTable.Grid` text column sorts `3333-2` before `3333-10`.

title: Vite+ 1.5 and the renamed Workers test plugin, clearing the last HIGH dev-server advisory
entry:
**The toolchain moves to Vite+ 1.5.0, and the Workers test pool to its renamed successor.** `vite-plus` 0.1.24 and the Vite 8.0.16 it brought carried GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm (HIGH, CVSS 7.5) and four lower advisories (GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv, GHSA-r825-w8mm-5pxw, GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22, GHSA-9jrq-w75r-8gcw), fixed only from vite-plus 1.1. Vite+ 1.x runs upstream Vitest instead of the rebundled `@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-test`, so the catalog's `vitest` is now 5.1.0, the version vite-plus 1.5.0 depends on, and the `vitest` alias leaves the `overrides`. `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` 0.23.0 peered only Vitest 4; its successor `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` 1.6.0 keeps the same `cloudflareTest()` plugin and `cloudflare:test` module, so every worker's `package.json`, `vitest.config.ts` and `worker-env.d.ts` change only the package name. The design-system story tests import the Playwright provider from `@vitest/browser-playwright`, now a catalog pin kept equal to `vitest`, because upstream Vitest has no `vitest/browser-playwright` entry.

**One Vite in the tree, at last.** The `vite` override alone never reached a `vite` peer: the alias reports its own version (1.5.0), which no `^8` peer range accepts, so pnpm auto-installed upstream Vite for SvelteKit, the Svelte and Tailwind plugins, Storybook and Vitest — the Vite 8.0.16 the advisories named. The root `package.json` now declares `vite` as the same alias, so every peer resolves to it, and `peerDependencyRules.allowedVersions` silences the version warnings that leaves (`vite`, and Storybook's optional `vite-plus` peer, which still names only 0.1/0.2). The lockfile was resolved fresh to drop the stale peer resolutions; outside the toolchain the only version that moved is `@types/react` 19.2.17 to 19.3.0.

**Two overrides leave.** `zod` was there only to reach the 4.4.3 the old pool hard-pinned; the new plugin pins 4.6.6, past the 4.6.6 floor. `tinypool@2` pinned 2.1.2 under the formatter; oxfmt 0.76 and Vitest 5.1 both pin 2.2.0, and the override would now drag them back. Oxfmt 0.76 and oxlint 1.91 come with the move: the formatter now hugs a single arrow-function argument that carries a return-type annotation and indents a list item's continuation line that opens inside an inline code span, which reformats 58 files (8 source, 50 Markdown), and oxlint-tsgolint 7 reports more `no-unnecessary-type-assertion` and `consistent-function-scoping` warnings (none are errors).

**`@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` is patched so the API worker's suite can run under Vitest 5.** When each test file after the first starts, Vitest 5 asks the pool for a snapshot of the modules the server has already transformed. workerd cannot read the host disk, so the plugin inlines every one of them into a single WebSocket reply. For the API worker that reply is about 65 MB across 4,254 modules, and workerd closes the socket with 1009 "Message is too large". The runtime then restarts in a loop that leaks a Vite server each time, until the run reaches about 14 GB. `patches/@cloudflare__vitest-plugin@1.6.0.patch` answers that one request with an empty map, so modules are fetched one at a time, as under Vitest 4. With the patch, all 319 API-worker test files pass (2,959 tests). Plugin 1.6.1 carries the same code, so the patch stays until a release bounds or chunks the reply.

title: Notifications is the one grid, with read and dismissed kept apart
entry:
**The notification centre is the product's one grid.** `apps/web/src/routes/(app)/notifications`
renders on `DataTable.Grid` with a declared column model (`notification-columns.ts`): a leading
read-state check, Notification, Details, Matter, Category, Priority and When, with Dismiss or Restore
pinned to the trailing edge on every row. The Everything/Unread toggle and the category select are
gone; their questions are the Status and Category column filters. The feed reads unread and read
rows together (`state` on `GET /api/v1/notifications` now repeats), and the dismissed rows are a
second read the member opens from the foot of the table, ordered after the live rows and drawn
quiet. New route `POST /api/v1/notifications/{id}/restore` returns a dismissed row to the feed as
read. Priority shows only Urgent or Needs Attention; informational rows have no word. The bell tray
leads with the most pressing of its rows, says "No Results" when empty, and links to "Open
Notifications". The `email.filed` kind now reads "Email saved to a matter".

title: The New Packet form can add the container it needs
entry: **The New Packet form can add the container it needs.** Nothing in `apps/web` called `POST /api/v1/custody/locations`, so a firm that had never set up storage met an empty, disabled Container list, and since Container is required the packet could never be saved. The Custodian screens' refusal for "no open container" only fired when containers existed and were all closed, so the zero-container case slipped through to the dead form. The Container field is now a combobox over every open container's path (`container-picker.svelte`) whose add row opens a panel for Name, Kind and Inside; `container-draft.ts` decides the requests, creating an office's own root node first when a container goes into an office the tree has never met, since only a root may name a firm office. An empty tree opens the panel by itself, the "no open container" refusal is gone from both Custodian screens, the required fields come first, and the commit reads Save.

title: The gate runs hosted again: ci.yml runs pnpm gate as the required check, with PR upkeep and Preview cleanup beside it
Give a directory record a More menu: copy link, email link, download contact card
entry: **A directory record has a More menu: copy its link, email it, or download it as a contact card.** `ActionDialog` takes an optional `menu` snippet, drawn first in its header controls as the same EllipsisVertical "More" dropdown the record window's kind's menu uses, so a record reads alike in either shell. The entity window fills it with Copy Link, Email Link and Download Contact Card; `contact-card.ts` builds a vCard 4.0 from the record and its contact points (name, a person's date of birth, and only the permitted, non-former emails, numbers and addresses), saved through `saveExport`.

title: Add a page menu beside the favourite star on every screen header
entry: **A page menu beside the favourite star on every screen header.** `ScreenHeader` draws `page-actions-menu.svelte` next to `FavoriteControl` whenever the screen is favoritable: Copy Link and Open in New Tab on every page, then a screen's own items passed through the new `pageMenu` snippet. Notifications moves What You Hear About, Shipping & Postage moves Postage Account, and Uploads moves Clear History into it. The star stays on the row, so the favourite state stays visible; the ruling is in `docs/conventions/design-corrections.md`.

title: Meetings: background blur's Rust path runs the segmentation model at 13 ms, exact, once one custom operator is added
entry: **Background blur's Rust path has its first number.** The owner chose to build blur memory-safely, Rust first, on 2026-11-09, and asked for image backgrounds on the same mask. The first slice-2 measurement is recorded as an amendment to `docs/research/2026-09-20-browser-media-effects.md`. `tract-tflite` cannot load MediaPipe's SelfieSegmenter as it stands, because of one custom operator, `Convolution2DTransposeBias`. With a small safe-Rust handler for that operator, the model runs in `wasm32` with SIMD at a p95 of 13.3 ms per inference and matches the reference interpreter exactly. The module is 2.17 MB gzipped, over the 1.5 MB budget. The `meetings.backgrounds-and-noise` ledger node records both rulings and drops its `awaiting-owner` question.

title: An address can be chosen rather than typed: the street box offers real addresses, from the platform's own index in the United States and Smarty elsewhere
entry:
Address autocomplete: the street box of the one address form offers real addresses as a person types, and choosing one fills the rest of the form.

**The United States is answered from the platform's own index.** A build Container indexes OpenAddresses every month into a platform R2 bucket — four census-region splits, about 62 bytes an address — and a query Container that sleeps when nobody is typing reads them by range. There is no per-lookup bill, no quota and no attribution badge, and what is typed never leaves the platform's account. The engine ranks addresses in the region the form already holds, or in the caller's primary office's region, first, without hiding the rest, and a chosen address comes back with its coordinates for whatever later needs a map. Sources whose recorded licence is share-alike, non-commercial or a bespoke agreement are left out, and every build records which sources it used.

**Every other country goes to Smarty, when its key pair is set.** Smarty was chosen on storage terms rather than coverage or price: the address a person picks is written into a permanent record, and of the large autocomplete services one lets a customer keep only its own place identifier while another treats every result as temporary.

A building with many units is offered as one line with a count, and choosing it offers the units in turn, because writing the building's line into a record whose client lives in unit 4B is a letter that does not arrive.

The Worker serves it through two read-shaped POSTs rather than GETs. Its invocation log records every request's full URL, query string included, and what is being sent is a client's address a few characters at a time; a body is not in that log. What the Worker counts is which operation ran, which engine served it and how it came out — nothing that could carry an address.

**Dormant until provisioned.** With neither engine provisioned, every answer is "unavailable" and the address form behaves exactly as before. The platform's index switches on when the `magna-carta-addresses` bucket exists, the address worker is deployed, and the app worker gains its `ADDRESS_SERVICE` binding; the first daily cron after that builds the index. Smarty switches on with `SMARTY_AUTH_ID` and `SMARTY_AUTH_TOKEN`. No deploy waits on either.

title: Firms choose from the current Claude models, with effort levels, checked against Anthropic's own list, and Settings › AI scrolls once
entry: **The model catalog is the current Anthropic generation, the AI settings screen checks it against Anthropic's own model list, and the screen scrolls once.** `packages/inference/src/catalog.ts` is catalog version 4 (effective 2026-11-09): the reasoning roster is `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` alone, and by the owner's ruling no previous-generation model is offered (`claude-opus-4-8` and `claude-sonnet-4-6` leave; a firm that pinned one reads as following the platform, because the setting read is total); by the owner's decision the `most-capable` tier (the platform default) moves to `claude-opus-5-5` and `balanced` to `claude-sonnet-5-5`; the utility slot moves from `claude-haiku-4-5` (earliest published retirement 2026-10-15, past) to `claude-haiku-5-5`, which nothing called; every entry gains a `displayName`, and every provider model records the effort levels it accepts (`effortLevels`, all five of low, medium, high, xhigh and max) and its own `defaultEffort` (medium for Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, high for Sonnet 5.5), which the entry schema checks; and every lifecycle and confidentiality fact was re-read on 2026-11-09 from Anthropic's model-deprecations and zero-data-retention pages. The Fable line stays out: it requires 30-day retention and is refused under zero data retention. New `packages/inference/src/provider-roster.ts` reads `GET /v1/models` through the injected `HttpClient` and reconciles it with the catalog (per entry, published or not; uncurated models listed as awaiting verification, never selectable); `apps/api-worker/src/inference/provider-roster-source.ts` composes it with an optional `ANTHROPIC_MODELS_API_KEY` secret, a three-second timeout and the Workers Cache API (six hours on success, five minutes on failure), and logs a failed read through `logOperationFailed`. `GET /api/v1/firm/ai/settings` gains `models[].displayName`, `models[].published`, `models[].effortLevels`, `models[].defaultEffort` and a `provider` object. On the web surface, the model picker names models by their display name, the facts list gains Model, Effort Levels and Provider's Live List rows, the section's label and title are now "AI", and `SettingsScrollRegion` is now `relative`, so LoadingRegion's absolutely positioned announcer no longer stretches the shell's `<main>` into a second scrollbar (`apps/web/test/settings-scroll-region-containment.test.ts`).

title: Screens read the session and the matter record from the one query cache
entry:
**Screens stop re-reading the session, and arriving at a matter read a moment ago is instant.** `readSession` (`apps/web/src/lib/matters/matters-api.ts`), which about forty-five surfaces call on mount, now answers from the one query cache under the same key the (app) guard fills on the way in (`meGetQueryKey`), at the session-stable ceiling. Each of those screens used to pay a full `/api/v1/me` round trip, in series, before its own read could start. `readSession(fetch, { fresh: true })` and `sessionPermissions.reread` skip the cache for the one write that changes the session under a screen (the Beta Branch switch). A refusal is never cached. The (app) guard drops the cached session before sending somebody to the joining screen, so their return with a firm is judged on a fresh answer rather than bounced back on the cached "no firm yet".

The `/matters/[id]` layout reads the matter through the cache at the record staleness (`readMatterRecord`, `apps/web/src/lib/matters/matter-record.ts`) when arriving, and from the server when the matter already on screen is re-read (`invalidateAll` after a status change or a renumbering). Recording where the paper file is kept drops the cached record. Home starts the Today card's reads from its route load, so the hover preload begins them before the click.

title: Partner and Associate as sub-roles of Attorney, and Owner/Admin renamed Admin
entry:
**Roles can have sub-roles; Partner and Associate are seeded under Attorney, and Owner/Admin is
renamed Admin.** `role.parent_role_id` names a parent. A member who holds a sub-role also holds the
parent as its own `member_role` row, so every read that joins `member_role` to `role_permission`
sees the parent's permissions unchanged, and a sub-role's grants are only what it adds. The
set-roles route refuses a sub-role without its parent and two sub-roles of one parent (problem type
`role-family`); the invite consumer assigns the parent alongside. Partner adds `reports:financial`,
`reports:productivity`, `time:viewFirm`, `time:approve`, `costs:approve` and `matters:reopen`;
Associate adds nothing yet. Rate capture now picks the timekeeper's role deterministically
(`readTimekeeperRateRole` in `packages/timekeeping/src/rate-resolution.ts`: sub-role, then a role
with sub-roles, then name) instead of an unordered `LIMIT 1`, and a sub-role with no rate falls back
to its parent's before the card default. Roles and Permissions and Users list each sub-role under its
parent (`apps/web/src/lib/members/role-families.ts`).

title: A person is entered and read on one scrolling page
entry: **A directory person is one scrolling page, entered and read alike.** `record-sections.svelte` stacks every section of a record on one page with a jump rail that lights the section in view (`record-sections.ts` holds the scroll arithmetic and the Show All cap), and both the New Person dialog and the entity window compose it in place of vertical tabs. Pronouns and Dates fold into one About section; `personDraftSummary` reads the draft back as values rather than counts; the entity window's facts move into `entityWindowSubtitle` and its context pane is passed only when a host hands over standing, so `entityWindowFacts` is gone; the matters and relationship panes cap at five rows with Show All; New Person's commit says Save.

title: Meetings appears under Communications: the rail reads the session's own permissions
entry: **The Meetings row reaches the rail.** The row is gated on `meetings:join`, and the rail and the palette asked `grantedPermissions()` in `apps/web/src/lib/tools/tool-permissions.ts`, a fixed mock list of tool permissions that never named it, so the row was filtered out for every member. That function now unions in the permissions the bootstrap session carries (registry-checked, additive only), and the `(app)` layout starts the shared single-flight session read so the gate does not wait on some screen asking first. Held by `apps/web/test/session-granted-destinations.test.ts`.

title: The calendar screen reads its date as a heading, with one View menu and three firm calendars
entry: **The calendar screen: one View menu, the date as its heading, and three firm calendars.** `calendar-toolbar.svelte` leads with the arrows and the window's name as a heading that opens `MonthJump` (new in `@magna-carta/design-system/calendar`, beside a `compact` density of `Calendar` that the rail's month now uses), and ends with Today and one View menu carrying the views, the week and day's concurrency choice and the agenda's Hide settled. The Kinds filter and `schedule-narrowing.ts` are removed. `calendar-sources.ts` splits the firm's records into `caseSettings` and `deadlines` sources, each with its own read in `calendar-reads.ts`; every rail name is Title Case. `CalendarGrid.Month` keeps its caption for assistive technology only when it has nothing to say, so a month that fills its host no longer overflows it by the caption's line. `formatMonthName` joins the civil-date formatters. Deadline sources read "Court Order" and "Firm".

title: Closing a matter sets the paper file's destruction date, no earlier than a firm minimum
entry: **Closing a matter asks for the date its paper file may be destroyed after, no earlier than a firm-set minimum, and the date shows on the calendar.** New per-firm table `matter_file_retention` (`20261109T180511_a-matter-file-carries-its-destruction-date.sql`): one row per matter keyed by `matter_id`, `destroy_on` under the shared civil-date shape CHECK, who recorded it and when, and a `(destroy_on, matter_id)` index for the firm-wide window. A table rather than a column because a CHECK on `matter` is a rebuild of the table most of the schema points at. `packages/matters/src/matter-file-retention.ts` composes the write: `isCivilDate` refuses a day that does not exist (`invalid-file-destruction-date`), an unknown matter or the platform's holding matter is `matter-not-found`, null deletes the row, and every write audits `matter.file_destruction_date.set` or `.cleared` with `{ previousDestroyOn, destroyOn }` because the row only ever holds the current date. `POST /api/v1/matters/{id}/close` takes an optional body `{ fileDestroyOn }` (a civil date, or null for none) and writes the date in the close's own batch; `composeFileDestructionDateAtClose` refuses a date earlier than the close plus the firm's `matters.fileRetentionMinimumYears` (`file-destruction-date-before-minimum`, naming the earliest date; 0, the default, is no minimum; a close on 29 February counts to 1 March), and a later date or none is always accepted. Reopening clears the date in the reopen's batch, audited. `PUT /api/v1/matters/{id}/file-destruction-date` (behind `matters:edit`, idempotent) changes it afterwards on a closed matter only (`matter-not-closed` otherwise), under the same floor. `GET`/`PATCH /api/v1/matters/settings` read and write the minimum; the PATCH needs the new `matters:manageRetention` permission, seeded to Owner/Admin in the same migration, and audits `matters.settings.updated`. The web gains **Settings › File Retention**; `MatterDetail` gains `fileDestructionDate`. The `matterFileDestruction` timeline source (kind `fileDestruction`, matter-anchored, no label) puts the date on the federated read, the web calendar's **File destruction dates** layer stops being a Soon row and reads it under the same `layer:fileDestruction` key, and the matter's Activity section names it. The close step's right panel gains a **Paper File** section, **Destroy After** (prefilled at the earliest allowed date) or **No Destruction Date**. On the status window of a closed matter, **Destroy After** is a date field with **Record** and **Clear**: unlike the office it is not saved as the field changes, because a segmented date field holds a complete wrong date at each keystroke of a typed year. The platform derives no date and nothing deletes anything when one arrives.

title: Settings › Text: choose the typeface you read in, and the whole interface follows
entry: **The reading typeface is a live user axis.** Settings · Text's Font Family row, a Soon seam until now, applies one of five faces instantly: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (default), Lexend, OpenDyslexic, Literata (the one serif reading profile) and the system face. A `typeface` resolver modifier in `packages/design-tokens/resolver.json` emits `:root[data-typeface="…"]` overlays that re-point `--mc-font-sans` only; Tailwind's `--font-sans` now maps onto that variable in `tailwind.template.css` instead of the inlined stack, so `font-sans` and the document default follow the choice. The preference rides the existing theme-preference seam (`magna-carta.typeface`), the no-flash boot script in `apps/web/src/app.html` mirrors it, and the change ledger and Restore work as on Accessibility. The three new faces are self-hosted OFL Fontsource packages declared in `fonts.css`; a browser fetches their files only when a person picks one. The developer appearance module now passes the axes it has no switcher for through unchanged instead of resetting contrast and scroll-edge markers to their defaults.

title: The Changelog in the profile menu opens a real page, built from the public changelog
entry: **The profile menu's Websites > Changelog opens an in-app Changelog screen at `/updates`.** `apps/web/src/routes/(app)/updates/+page.svelte` renders `docs/public-changelog.md`, imported as text into the web bundle and parsed by `buildPublicChangelogArtifact` from `@magna-carta/product-updates` (now an `apps/web` dependency), so every build carrying an `audience: public` fragment updates the screen with no further step. Entries are grouped by date and category with a category filter; their Markdown is read by a small inline parser (`apps/web/src/lib/product-updates/changelog-text.ts`) into nodes rendered as plain Svelte text, never `{@html}`, and repository-relative links keep only their words. `EcosystemSite` gains an optional `route`: while a site's `href` is null, the profile menu and the command palette open that in-app screen instead of showing "Soon".

title: Split Firm Brand out of Firm Profile; move Rooms and Resources under Firm
entry: **Firm Profile is the firm's name alone; the marks moved to a new Firm Brand page, and Rooms and Resources moved under Firm.** `settings/firm-profile/+page.svelte` drops its offices plate (a copy of the Offices register) and its brand-images plate; the plate moved unchanged to `settings/firm-brand/`, registered as the `firm-brand` section in `apps/web/src/lib/settings/settings-sections.ts` and gated on the same `firm:manageProfile` the brand-image routes enforce. The `resources` section's group is now `firm`, and its catalog's actions column is one `DropdownMenu` behind an icon-sized trigger rather than a button per act.

title: Record a Deadline refuses a time that is not a time, and no longer offers No matter
entry: **Record a Deadline no longer accepts a time that is not a time, and no longer offers "No matter".** The deadline form's time was a plain text box that took anything typed into it and said nothing until the commit refused; it is now the same time-of-day control the event form uses (`apps/web/src/lib/calendar/record-deadline-dialog.svelte`). A half-typed time reports an empty value from that control, so the form reads the control's `validity.badInput` and the draft refuses it (`deadlineDraftShortfalls(draft, { timeEntryUnfinished })` in `apps/web/src/lib/calendar/deadline-draft.ts`) instead of recording the deadline as due at the end of the day, and the refusal is shown beneath the field with `aria-invalid` once the reader leaves it. The server already refused a malformed `dueAtTime` at the request contract and in `assertWallClockTime`; tests now pin both (`apps/api-worker/test/calendar-routes.test.ts`, `packages/calendar/test/deadline-service.test.ts`). The shared matter picker gains `offerNoMatter` (default on), which the deadline form turns off: a deadline is recorded only on a matter (`matter_deadline.matter_id` is `NOT NULL` and the only create route is `POST /api/v1/matters/{matterId}/deadlines`), so the list no longer offers an answer the commit then refused with "A matter is needed."

title: Only an administrator can change the firm's postage account, and the fee on a label is the server's number
entry:
**Only an administrator can connect, replace or disconnect the firm's postage account, and the
platform's fee on a label is the server's number, not the caller's.** Two findings from a security
review of shipping, both closed before any firm could reach them.

**The account.** The connect and disconnect routes were gated on `shipping:manage` — the same
permission as drafting a shipment — and the credential store does no check of its own on a write, by
design, because it defers to the route. So any member who could draft a shipment could replace the
firm's EasyPost key with one on an account they control, and every shipment an administrator bought
afterwards, with its clients' names and addresses, would go to that account; or disconnect the firm's
postage outright. Both routes now require `firm:manageSecrets`, the right the Settings navigation
already tagged the page "View" without — but whose controls the page itself never checked, so it also
now shows that member the account's health and a sentence saying only an administrator can change it,
instead of a key field the server would refuse. Reading whether an account is connected stays on
`shipping:manage`, since the register uses it to tell exactly that member when no account is
connected. Not reachable under the
default roles, where only Owner/Admin holds `shipping:manage`.

**The fee.** `POST /api/v1/shipments/{id}/purchase` took `serviceFeeMinor` from the request, with no
upper bound, and a positive fee becomes a billable charge on the shipment's matter when the firm
recovers the shipping service fee. A member who could buy a label could put any amount on a client's
bill without `costs:track`. The field is gone from the request, and the fee is set on the server:
zero, since the platform charges nothing per label today. A client that still sends it has it
ignored rather than refused, so a browser tab left open on the old page can still buy its label.

Both are pinned by tests that fail when the hole is put back.

title: The lockfile records the zod override the manifests now name, so a frozen install passes again
Every dependency on its newest safe release: Wrangler 4.158, zip 9 across the Rust engines, and twelve HIGH/CRITICAL advisories cleared
entry:
**Every npm dependency is on its newest compatible release, Wrangler is on 4.158.0, and every Cargo lockfile is refreshed.** The catalog in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` moves each pin to the newest release on its own major line that is past the three-day cooldown, including `wrangler` 4.110.0 to 4.158.0 (Worker Previews need 4.135.0 or later), `@cloudflare/workers-types` to `5.20261106.1`, `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` to 0.23.0, `better-auth` to 1.7.18, `zod` to 4.6.7, `svelte` to 5.57.3, `bits-ui` to 2.20.6 and Storybook to 10.6.6. `happy-dom` crosses to 21.0.4, the first release clear of two HIGH advisories (an import-alias escape to host code and an SSRF through parsed iframes and stylesheets). Two overrides are new: `tinypool@2` at 2.1.2 clears two CRITICAL prototype-pollution-to-code-execution records reached through `vite-plus`'s formatter, and `zod` at 4.6.7 reaches the copy the Workers test pool hard-pins at 4.4.3. Upstream bits-ui now restores the body's style through CSSOM, so `patches/bits-ui@2.20.6.patch` keeps only the preventable-`onFocusOutside` half. better-auth 1.7 types the two-factor enrolment answer as a union with an emailed-code shape, which `apps/web/src/lib/account/two-factor.ts` now refuses by name. Svelte 5.57 flags the safe-browse canvas's deliberate `role="application"`, now ignored with its reason beside it. Terrazzo 2.10 writes zero-length shadow lengths more compactly, so `packages/design-tokens/generated/` is regenerated with no change in meaning. `yara-x` moves to 1.23, which requires wasmtime 48, so the accepted `RUSTSEC-2026-0269` entry leaves `osv-scanner.toml`.

**The Rust supply chain crosses the majors that carried advisories.** Every `zip` consumer in `crates/` and `containers/*` moves to 9.4.1, which clears nine zip advisories (several of them CRITICAL: a dual-header parser differential, an AES-entry HMAC bypass, extraction outside the target directory). zip 9 returns entry names as a `Result`, and each call site falls back to a lossy decode of the raw name, so no entry is skipped. `tantivy` 0.27 lifts `lru` to 0.18.5 (RUSTSEC-2026-0253). Also moved: the RustCrypto family (aes 0.9, cbc 0.2, md-5/sha1/sha2 0.11 and the rest, with cipher 0.5's trait renames), `cfb` 0.16, `chardetng` 1.0, `zune-png` 0.5, `tower-http` 0.7, `base64` 0.23, `lopdf` 0.46 and `oar-ocr` 0.9.2. Held, each for a stated reason: `lopdf` 0.47 rebuilds a missing cross-reference table on load and so reports a broken file as intact; `hayro` 0.9 replaces the device trait the bad-redaction detector implements; `quick-xml` 0.42 rewrites the event model under the untrusted OOXML walk; `sevenz-rust2` 0.25 makes private the internals the 7z parser reads; `reqwest` 0.13's rustls feature pulls in `aws-lc-sys`, a C library; `mail-parser` 1.0 needs rustc 1.98; and `rand` 0.10 is held because `ms-offcrypto-writer` takes a rand 0.9 generator.

title: The api worker becomes a manifest of domain modules, with an HTTP and background seam and four checks that hold its shape
entry: **The api worker gets a design for a shape that grows by domain.** A spec and a proposed decision reorganize the Worker's 99 flat route files into about twenty domain modules, each a sub-app built by one constructor and mounted by a short manifest, with a route's request and response shapes moving to the domain package and the tree split into an HTTP side and a background side held apart by a fitness test. Four repo-wide checks are specified to stop the shape regrowing, and `wrangler check startup` joins the gate as a recorded trend. Lazy per-domain loading was checked and deferred: Hono's router refuses additions after its first match, and domains do not map to path prefixes. The standing ruling that the background orchestration stays in this Worker is kept. Step 1 of the migration is built in the same change: the `Bindings` type, the per-env auth instance and the per-env logger leave `app.ts` for modules of their own (so no consumer imports the app module), `createDomainApp()` becomes the one router constructor, the four fitness tests hold today's tree with every current offender on a ledger that only shrinks, and `pnpm gate` gains a `startup` dimension that records the worker's local startup span as a trend. Step 2 follows in the same change: the 107 route files move into 21 domain directories, each a sub-app mounted by a manifest `app.ts` iterates; the hand-maintained list of every operation becomes one committed list per domain, emitted through the contract pipeline and held per module by the conformance suite; the area note's per-surface rules move beside their modules; and the emitted contract is proved identical after a canonical key sort, so the snapshot and the client carry a reordering only. Step 3 follows: the tree splits into `src/http/` and `src/background/`, every consumer and sweep under its subsystem's name on the background side, and the boundary test becomes directory-based with no allow-list left. Step 4 begins with the calendar: its 42 request and response shapes and 11 response envelopes move to `packages/calendar/src/contract.ts` as plain zod named with `.meta({ id })`, the emitted contract stays byte-identical, and the two helpers a package-side shape needs move beside it (`identifierField` to `@magna-carta/identifiers/field`, the list envelopes to `@magna-carta/data-access/pagination-contract`). The directory follows: its 60 request and response shapes move to `packages/directory/src/contract.ts`, field descriptions included, and the contract stays byte-identical.
