sweep, all below the gate's fail threshold, so nothing had failed. All moved within their existing
major:

- `hono` 4.13.0 to 4.13.5 in the catalog, the only one with production reach: unbounded dot-notation
  nesting in `parseBody()` (a memory DoS through any form body), the query parser reading past a `#`
  fragment, and `toSSG()` writing outside its output directory.
- `devalue` pinned to 5.9.2 (a parser DoS on malformed input), through svelte, SvelteKit and
  sveltekit-superforms.
- `joi` 17 pinned to 17.13.8 (two prototype-pollution paths), reached only as superforms' optional
  validator adapter.
- `js-yaml` 4 to 4.3.2 and 3 to 3.15.2 (merge-key exhaustion), behind the OpenAPI client generator.
- `sharp` to 0.35.4 (an out-of-bounds read in its bundled libheif), behind miniflare.
- `extract-zip`'s two symlink-traversal advisories have **no fixed release**, so their carrier is
  removed instead. `@cloudflare/puppeteer` hard-pins `@puppeteer/browsers` 2.2.4 for its Node launcher,
  which downloads a local Chrome. A Worker never runs that launcher: the entry point drives the
  Browser Rendering binding, and a dry-run bundle of the API worker contains none of
  `@puppeteer/browsers`, `extract-zip` or `yauzl`. Removing it with a pnpm override drops about 600
  lockfile lines and adds no baseline entry.

**Account · Security adds, removes and re-issues two-factor. It was the account surface's last Soon
seam.** The sign-in screen had verified a code since the auth backend shipped, and no screen could set
one up. `$lib/account/two-factor.ts` wraps the plugin's `enable` → `verifyTotp`, `disable` and
`generateBackupCodes`, and words each refusal by its code. The add panel is one `ActionDialog` whose
three steps (password, authenticator, recovery codes) turn over in place and end on `"done"`. It is
offered only while the session says two-factor is off: in the pinned plugin, `enable` on an enrolled
account replaces the working secret and marks it verified with no code asked for.
`apps/api-worker/test/account-two-factor.test.ts` pins that behaviour and three other facts the page
relies on (the session reporting the change at once, a refused removal leaving it on, and replaced
recovery codes retiring the old set).

- **`QrCode` in the design system** (`@magna-carta/design-system/qr-code`), over `uqr`: pure
  TypeScript, no dependencies, and it returns the module matrix rather than markup. It is drawn as one
  SVG path in the chrome token pair, the one pair that stays dark-on-light in dark mode. Checked by
  decoding the rendered screenshots in both modes with an independent reader.
- **The authenticator issuer is "Magna Carta".** Unset, the plugin fell back to the library's
  `appName`, so a member's phone would have filed the account under "Better Auth". The fix is
  `TOTP_ISSUER` on the plugin, not the instance-wide `appName`.
- `account-seams` now guards the other direction: no account page claims a Soon badge or a control
  waiting on a backend.

title: Safe Website Viewer: download everything a capture found; measure whether the browser's country can be chosen
entry:
The Safe Website Viewer downloads everything a capture found, not only its picture. `capture-export.ts` builds one ZIP through `client-zip` (the bulk-download library): the screenshot PNG, `capture.txt` (every inspector tab as plain text, ordered as the tabs are) and `capture.json` (the view without its screenshot, plus capture time, duration, mode, the different-site flag and the registration record when the member opened that tab for the same host). Nothing in the archive is markup: addresses are written as text so a report opened later in a browser cannot be the thing that finally lets the page act. History entries now carry their mode, so the report says whether a held Live browser or a fresh Static one produced it.

`POST /api/v1/safe-browse/location-probe?country=US` — which country a website sees the Safe Website Viewer's isolated browser in, and whether that can be chosen.

The owner's first Live session surfaced in New Zealand. A page aimed at one country often shows its real content only to visitors from there, so a viewer that lands wherever the rendering service places it may be looking at the decoy. The service accepts a `location` when a browser session is launched, documented in one line that says neither whether it is honoured nor whether it moves the address a website sees; quick actions, the static capture's path, do not document it at all.

The probe reads the service's own trace endpoint three ways — a session with no location, a session launched with the requested country, and a quick action carrying it — and reports the country and data centre each time, with `sessionHonoursLocation` and `quickActionHonoursLocation` as the two facts a country picker stands on. It navigates only to that constant; its one input is a two-letter code. Audited and on the expensive rate-limit bucket, because each run holds two billed browsers.

title: A copy that leaves the platform has every tracked change accepted; the stored document keeps them
entry:
**A copy that leaves the platform has every tracked change accepted; the stored document keeps them.** A `.docx` version the browser editor cuts owes an export copy from the moment it exists (`export_copy_state`, `export_r2_key`, `export_size_bytes` on `file_version`, marked `pending` in the batch that cuts the version), and the copy is made off the request path: the save asks the shared per-firm queue directly (`file.export_copy_requested`), and the relay's publication of `file.version_committed` reaches the same idempotent handler as the backstop. `acceptTrackedChanges` in `@magna-carta/document-assembly` (`./ooxml-accept-tracked-changes`) is the pass — an XML rewrite over the revision elements of WordprocessingML, never a re-render: insertions keep their content, deletions go, a deleted paragraph mark joins its paragraph to the next keeping the following mark as Word does, deleted rows and cells go, property-change records and range markers go. A part with nothing recorded is left byte-for-byte; a version that recorded nothing is `ready` at its own key.

Every download lane is served from the copy through one resolver (`apps/api-worker/src/exports/export-object.ts`): the per-file redirect, and every lane of the bulk download with the entries' keys swapped once before the lanes branch. A copy still pending at the moment of a download is made on the spot; a bulk selection with more than three pending answers 409 `export-copies-pending`. A document past the pass's caps is recorded `unavailable` and downloads as stored, with the audit row saying so (`exportCopy` on the per-file audit, `acceptedCopies`/`unavailableCopies` on the bulk one). The enumeration of outbound paths, what is deliberately not one, and what must join the list when built, is in `apps/api-worker/src/editing/CLAUDE.md`. `readPackage` takes its caps as a parameter, with the template caps as the default; `export-copy` joins the matter-scoped object classes; the purge list carries the copy beside the version's object.

title: A trust account is reconciled on its own screen, the cushion and the unclaimed-funds file take forms, and every account states its position
entry:
**The build register renders on `main`, never on a branch.** `docs/now.md`, `docs/now.html` and `docs/decisions-open.html` were rendered by every branch that flipped a `roadmap.d/` node, so any two such branches rewrote the same whole document and conflicted on it: fifteen of the last forty merges to `main` touched the file, and a trust pull request hit the conflict three times in four days on a file nobody had written by hand. The register is a derived view of the trunk, so the trunk renders it, as it already did for `CHANGELOG.md` and the Decision-Log register: the per-merge assembly workflow when it has minutes, the weekly docs-sync routine otherwise. `tooling/doc-fragments/register-renderers.mjs` says who renders (`main`, `docs-assembly`, `docs-sync/*`); `vp run register-build` refuses to write anywhere else (`--preview` shows the render without committing it); and `pnpm run lint:roadmap` holds the files to a fresh render where they are rendered and fails a branch that carries a change to them, with the `git checkout` that restores them. A branch's whole change is its ledger edit.

**Trust, second round.** The reconciliation workbench lands on the firm's Trust screen and its own route (`apps/web/src/routes/(app)/trust/reconciliations/[reconciliationId]`): a statement recorded by hand with its lines, or imported through the preview-then-confirm pair quoting the preview's fingerprint; a reconciliation opened on a statement; the three-way proof as it stands beside what a closed one froze; unmatched lines beside outstanding items with the suggestions' signals marked; matching and withdrawing by hand; closing the proof balanced or not. The cushion's three acts are forms behind `trust:firmFunds`. The unclaimed-funds file is a section of the account's record, reading dormancy against a day the reader states. Three backend additions: `GET /api/v1/trust/accounts/{id}/position` (book, client total, held, cushion, counts, from dated rows through the proof's own leg computation), `GET /api/v1/trust/reconciliations/{id}/matches` (withdrawals included), and the matter's number and title on each queued request.

title: The create control holds one more character, so Documents draws
entry:
**The template library rendered as the crash screen on every visit.** `CreateControl` refuses a noun longer than its fixed width holds, `/documents` shipped `noun="Template"` against a budget of seven, and the refusal is a `throw` raised while the screen renders — so the render boundary replaced the whole page and the defect read as a 500 rather than a label that did not fit.

The owner's ruling was to re-measure the one width: `size.create-control` is 140px (was 136px) and `CREATE_NOUN_MAX_LENGTH` is eight (was seven), so every create control in the product moves together rather than one screen stretching the control for its own label. The budget is written down as the measurement it is — "New Template" sets 81.6px in the reading face at the small size, and a 140px control leaves 80px of label after the padding, the glyph and its gap.

Two gates now read a noun before it renders. `pnpm run lint:matter-create-control` read create nouns only out of the matter section registry, where they are declared as data, and never out of a screen's own markup, where this one was written; it reads both now and names the file and line. `apps/web/test/documents-library-screen.test.ts` mounts the screen under the real root layout, so a render-time throw of any kind there fails in the battery instead of on the deployed site.

title: Live browsing: follow a suspect link through its steps in one held isolated browser
entry:
**Follow a suspect link through its steps: the viewer's Live mode.** The safe website viewer's Live
toggle stops being a Soon affordance. Static still opens every address in a fresh isolated browser;
Live keeps one per member, held by a `SafeBrowseSession` Durable Object keyed `firmId:userId`, so a
shortener into a consent wall into a credential form can be walked to its third step — which exists
only because the first two set cookies. The object holds the remote browser's session id, never the
handle and never any browsing history; an idle alarm (three minutes) and an age ceiling (fifteen)
close the billed browser, and leaving Live or the page releases it through `sendBeacon` on
`pagehide`. A reconnect to a browser the service already reaped relaunches rather than failing, and
the screen says the cookies were dropped.

The live answer carries the capture's fields one for one, the redirect chain read off the navigation
the session actually made — so the inspector renders it unchanged, and never has to pad a missing
chain into a false "answered directly". Request interception guards **every navigation request the
browser makes**, in any frame, through `assertPublicTarget`: a refused sub-frame is blocked alone, a
refused main-frame hop fails the navigation with the generic refusal. Sub-resources are not resolved
one by one, the same line the static renderer draws. What crosses back is still a screenshot and
text, never markup, so nothing new reaches the member's device.

Decision: `docs/decisions/pending/interactive-browsing-on-a-per-member-session.md`. Pixel streaming
is not built; the probe showed it possible, and the reasons against it are not technical.

title: Account Settings says less and does more, and the dropdown takes the second one
entry:
**The account surface states facts and builds the controls its small text was standing in for.**
`SettingDefinition.description` is optional rather than required (owner correction, 2026-09-18) and
`SettingsRow` renders the muted line only where there is one; `AccountMasthead` lost its `meta` prop
outright, since all three of its pages were restating their own headings. Three of the four rows the
`account-seams` guard was written for are built, so that guard now tests the named seam rows
(Two-Factor) rather than disabling every control on a page that carries one.

- **Profile · Photo.** `member_photo` in the per-firm database keyed by the member's user id, bytes
  in the firm's bucket under their own SHA-256, `me.photo` / `me.setPhoto` / `me.removePhoto` and a
  content route beside them. Content-addressed and written object-first, the firm brand-image
  reasoning. Registered in the PII registry as a hard-delete at the subject, with the note that the
  row is the only thing naming the object.
- **Security · Password.** Better Auth's `/change-password` behind the product's action panel, with
  `revokeOtherSessions` offered and defaulted on. `password.changed` joins the auth audit through an
  endpoint after-hook — `internalAdapter.updateAccount` passes no context to the account hooks, so
  the endpoint is the only place the door has a name, and the hook guards on the returned value
  because an after-hook runs over failed requests too.
- **Profile · Identity.** The address is engraved from the session bootstrap. No change control: the
  decision and what a change would actually cost are in `docs/decisions/pending/`.

`advanced.ipAddress.ipAddressHeaders` now reads `cf-connecting-ip` ahead of `x-forwarded-for`. The
library's default reads the latter alone and, with no trusted-proxy list, refuses any multi-hop
value — which is the only shape Cloudflare sends — so every session recorded an empty address. The
signed-in-devices row omits the clause where one is genuinely absent, and `REVOCATION_LAG_NOTE` and
`UNRECORDED_ADDRESS` are gone with the banner and the caption that carried them.

`member-name-api.ts` moved onto the generated client and `member-photo-api.ts` was written on it, so
the `lint:screen-data` hand-written-transport budget stayed flat at 56; the adapter both use
(`outcomeOf`) lives at the seam.

**The honorific field takes a second pick.** It holds several on one comma-separated line and the
list narrows against the part after the last comma — which while somebody types is the word they are
typing and at rest was the honorific they had just chosen, so the list offered exactly the one entry
already held. The reading moved out of `honorific-field.svelte` into `$lib/names/honorific-line.ts`,
where `typedPart(query, typing)` makes a settled line narrow nothing and the pick sequence is pinned
step by step. Two smaller faults went with it: the rows now carry a per-pick sequence number in their
value, so the primitive's "clicking the row it already holds is a deselect" can never leave an act
unreported, and the empty string that deselect reports is no longer appended as a token — which used
to leave a dangling comma in somebody's stored name.

title: The address form can say a postal code reads wrong, and offer a state
entry:
The address form can now say a postal code reads wrong, and can offer a country's states, provinces or counties.

It could do neither before. The per-country table it renders from is a curated shape — which boxes a country uses, what they are called, what order they read in — and it carried no postal-code patterns and no administrative-area lists. The feature ledger has held that as the open question since the form shipped.

`@magna-carta/address-formats` is the missing half: 252 countries projected from the address-internationalization corpus into 182 postal-code formats and 62 administrative-area lists, 1,619 areas in all. The corpus is checked in and refreshed by a deliberate act rather than fetched at build time, so no build depends on a third party being up and no postal rule changes under a release nobody made. The generator validates as well as renders — every pattern must compile anchored and every published example must match its own pattern — so a bad corpus breaks the build rather than the address form.

The constraints reach the component as optional props, the way the country list already does. That is not ceremony: the design system links exactly one workspace package by design and `AddressFields` is domain-blind, so importing a corpus into it would end that for every consumer to serve two screens.

A malformed code renders as the field's hint and never its error, so the box is never marked invalid and nothing can refuse a commit — a code can match its country's published format perfectly and still reach nobody. "This country publishes no postal format" stays a different answer from "this is wrong"; seventy of the 252 fall in the first case. The region field takes a native datalist rather than a combobox, because it is not a closed choice: a combobox settles back onto a listed value on close, which would destroy an address in a place no published list carries.

Alongside it, `@magna-carta/address-lookup` adds the autocomplete port with no engine behind it yet — `suggest` and `resolve`, typed outcomes that never throw, and a deferred implementation that reports `engine-not-implemented`, the same wired-but-dormant shape the discovery search index takes. A surface written against it degrades to exactly today's behaviour with no branch and no flag to remove later.

No provider is adopted and nothing calls out. No address leaves the firm's tenancy.

title: The opening panel logs what the container did, stamps each stage with its own time, and names the stages plainly
entry: **The opening panel's stages are renamed, stamped with their own durations, and its details are the open's log rather than a second copy of the stages.** `DocumentEditorContainer` now records its phases (`requested`, `started`, `listening`, `served`, `stopped`, `error`) in its object's storage through a `fetch` override and the library's lifecycle hooks (`apps/edit-worker/src/container-phases.ts`), served at `/magna-carta/status` on the document's origin; the session object keeps every callback of an open, not only the last; and `GET …/edit-session/progress` carries both (`callbacks`, `container`), the container's record read over `EDIT_SERVICE` under a 1.5 s budget and null when the worker is unbound. `openFeed` stamps each line with its stage's own duration; `openLog` merges the three sides by instant into the rows the details show. The platform gives no sight of coolwsd's own output, so the boot shows as the gap between `started` and `listening`.

title: The back button shows the matter's number beside the arrow, and the About block reads as rows with the commit linked
entry:
**The Magna Carta block in the editor's About dialog reads as labelled rows, with the build linked to its commit.** The first cut ran its lines together inside the dialog's row class; `buildRows` now yields label, value and an optional `href`, the block renders a heading and one flex row per fact (`.mc-about-row`, `.mc-about-key`), and the stylesheet the edit worker serves lays them out. The commit links to `REPOSITORY_URL/commit/<hash>` in a new tab; a development build has no link.

**The back button on the editor's bar shows the matter's number beside the arrow.** The editor's shortcuts bar draws no words for any button (its builder switches labels off and keeps a button's text as its `data-cooltip` tooltip), so the number the host sent as the label was a tooltip and nothing more. The stylesheet the edit worker serves now draws the words from that attribute in a `::after` rule on the host button, cut to `BACK_LABEL_CHARACTERS` (12) with an ellipsis; the editor's own tooltip shows the whole number on hover.

title: Trust is a place you can go: the matter's ledger moves client money, and the sidebar opens the firm's accounts
entry: **Trust, first production round.** The matter's Trust section stops standing empty: `apps/web/src/lib/trust/matter-trust.svelte.ts` reads the firm's trust accounts, chooses one (the only open account, else the remembered one, else the first open one alphabetically), reads the matter's ledger against it — a 404 is "no ledger yet", a fact the surface states rather than a failure — and the three writes the section was designed around land as dialogs: a deposit, a payment out proposed under the firm's authorization posture (released at once or left pending with the eligible approvers named), and a transfer between two of the client's matters. Pending requests on the matter show in the notices band with approve, reject and withdraw. The sidebar's Trust row lights up over `apps/web/src/routes/(app)/trust`: the accounts register, the act that opens one, and per account the approval queue with its verbs, the statements and reconciliations as recorded, the bank-charge cushion, and the firm's authorization posture with its change. `POST /api/v1/trust/accounts` is the one route the slice lacked — every test had seeded an account through the domain package — and it derives the jurisdiction from the office rather than taking one. The trust-account listing now has one home, `$lib/trust/trust-api.ts`, which the report screen re-exports. The reconciliation workbench, statement entry and import, funding the cushion, and the unclaimed-funds file remain backend-only and say so on the screen.

title: The editor's About dialog names the platform's build; the container settles on standard-1 with the audit off
entry:
**The editor's About dialog names the platform's build.** `apps/edit-worker/src/editor-about.ts` appends a block to `#about-dialog-info-container` as the page streams through, after the editor's own version rows: the edit worker's baked-in build identity (`@magna-carta/build-identity`), which is the deploy's commit since every Worker in one deploy reports the same one; a development build says so. The stylesheet the worker already serves gives the block its spacing.

**The editor container settles on `standard-1`, and the image switches the server audit off.** After a week of sizes: `standard-4` cleared the audit's hardware warning and felt no different to use, so the owner kept the smallest size on 2026-09-20 and accepted the warning as the stated consequence. The warning counts as an error to the audit, and with `IsAdminUser` true for every member it would put the "Check warnings of your server" snackbar over every open, so `disable_server_audit=true` joins `extra_params`; there is no per-line switch. Taking it out for one deploy brings the audit back for a diagnosis. `docs/operating-costs.md` carries the sizes and what each buys.

title: Meetings: a video meeting or an audio call starts from any calendar event, and the sidebar gains a Communications group
entry:
**A call is a meeting made of sound, not a video meeting with the camera off.** `meeting.medium`
(`video` | `audio`, `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'video'`, CHECK) joins the per-firm lineage as an additive
`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` — a rebuild is impossible on a parent table, so the column carries its
own CHECK, which `packages/database/CLAUDE.md` proves is allowed there. `POST /api/v1/meetings` takes
an optional `medium`, `MeetingSummary` carries it on every read including the list, and the creation
audit row carries it as a closed-vocabulary label beside the identifiers.

**The medium is chosen at Start and never changed**, and the room is what holds that: the signaling
socket is told which kind of gathering it is off the meeting row — never off anything a browser
says — and a `publish` naming a camera or a screen share in a call is `refused` with
`track-kind-refused`, the socket kept open and nothing asked of the routing service. One meeting per
event means the first Start decides; a second Start asking for the other medium gets the room that
exists, with `created: false`, rather than switching a camera on for everybody already in it.

**Two room fixes from the same review.** The grace period after a dropped connection is now timed
per person, on the participant's own roster entry: one pending deadline for the room was a grace
period only for whoever armed it, so the second person to drop was swept while twenty seconds into
their own minute. And a stay now holds **one live socket, newest wins** — an upgrade retires the
older socket (`refused: superseded`, then a 4000 close), resets the participant to no session and no
tracks, and tells the room. That is forced by WebRTC rather than chosen: a reconnecting browser
brings a new peer connection, so it cannot resume the routing session its predecessor opened, and
carrying the old one forward left the returning member publishing where nobody was subscribed while
everybody else held a subscription to a session that would never send again — a black tile that
never resolved.

**A session handle means nothing without the room that issued it.** The whole fleet's meetings run
inside one Cloudflare Realtime application, which knows nothing about meetings or firms: it will
forward any session's track to anybody presenting the application credential. The signaling room was
passing a browser's `subscribe` frame straight through, so any participant in any meeting could pull
any other meeting's media — including another firm's — by naming a session id. The room now checks
every (session, track) pair against its OWN roster and refuses the whole frame (`unknown-track`)
without asking the service anything, refuses a subscription to the asker's own session, and refuses a
`publish` whose track name does not carry the publisher's own participant handle
(`foreign-track-name`) — a name is how every other browser resolves a track to a tile, so a foreign
one puts one member's camera under another member's face. Published tracks are recorded from what the
service CONFIRMED rather than from what the browser offered, and a participant is capped at eight.

**The room now closes what it started.** Each published track's media section is kept beside its name,
which is the only handle the routing service accepts for stopping one — so leaving, ending, closing a
track, and the new grace sweep all stop the forwarding they are ending, best-effort and never
blocking the record. A closed track leaves the roster and the room is told, where before a stopped
screen share was offered to every browser that joined afterwards.

**A closed laptop now ends a stay.** Nothing closed attendance when a socket simply went away, so a
stay stayed open for the life of the record. A dropped socket with no other socket for that stay arms
a Durable Object alarm a minute out; the sweep closes the stay through the firm-scoped data-access
layer with its own `meetings.meeting.left` audit row carrying `reason: socket-lost`, drops the roster
entry and stops the media. It never ends the meeting — that is the host's act and it records who took
it. The same alarm retires the ended marker a day after a meeting closes.

**An upgrade joins a participant; it does not reset one.** A reconnect or a second tab overwrote the
participant's routing session and tracks with nulls, leaving live media nothing could name, subscribe
to or close; and closing one of two sockets removed the participant the other was still watching
through. Both are read-modify-write under the object's own gate now, and a stay survives while any
socket for it is open.

**One participant's bad luck no longer ends the meeting.** The routing session was opened inside
`blockConcurrencyWhile`, and Cloudflare terminates and resets an object whose callback throws —
dropping every socket in the room. The failure is carried out as a value and answered on the one
socket that asked, and `end()` now writes its two storage operations under one gate so no frame can
land in the window that answered "the room does not know you" for a meeting that had just ended.

**The database holds the two rules the reads cannot.** A partial unique index on
`meeting_attendance (meeting_id, user_id) WHERE left_at IS NULL` and a capacity-guarded
`INSERT … SELECT` settle the races a read-then-write is a round trip too early for: a double-clicked
Join is handed the stay the first click opened, a thirteenth simultaneous arrival is told the room is
full, and the loser of a simultaneous Start is handed the winner's room — each of which previously
surfaced as a 500 on a raw constraint.

**Signaling is refused cross-origin, failures are recorded, and the attendance record is paged.** A
browser will open a WebSocket cross-origin carrying the member's cookie where it would refuse to let
that page read any other call here, so an upgrade whose `Origin` is not this application's is now a 403. Every routing-service and relay-credential failure goes through the standard error pipeline with
an Error ID — carried on the `refused` frame so the screen can show it — and never the upstream body,
the application id or a session description. `GET /api/v1/meetings/{id}/attendance` is cursor-paged
like every other list, and the relay-credential mint has one home
(`apps/api-worker/src/realtime/turn-credentials.ts`) shared by the meeting join and the connection
tool, each deciding its own fallback.

**Meetings, slice 1: a members-only video meeting started from a calendar event.** Media goes from the browser to the Cloudflare Realtime selective forwarding unit and never through a Worker; a `MeetingRoom` Durable Object per meeting brokers each browser's session with the unit over hibernating WebSockets, keeps the roster and writes attendance. `@magna-carta/meetings` holds the domain half on the communications package's shape, two tables join the per-firm lineage, and the routes sit under the chokepoint behind `meetings:host` and `meetings:join`.

A meeting belongs to exactly one calendar event and carries no title, time or participant list of its own — those are the event's, read through a join — so authorization, visibility and the walled-matter question are answered once, by the event, rather than a second time by a free-standing meeting object. One meeting per event by unique index, created on demand by the first member who presses Start. The record keeps who was in the room and when, and nothing that was said: no recording, no transcript, no chat, which is what lets the feature ship before the jurisdiction consent machinery exists. Without `REALTIME_SFU_APP_ID` and `REALTIME_SFU_APP_SECRET` the create and join routes answer 503 and the calendar shows no Start control, so an unprovisioned account sees the feature dormant rather than broken. Design: [`docs/specs/2026-09-18-meetings-design.md`](docs/specs/2026-09-18-meetings-design.md).

External guests, recording, dial-in by telephone and rooms larger than the slice-1 cap of twelve are each their own node in the feature ledger, sequenced after this one.

**The sidebar gains a Communications group** (owner ruling, 2026-09-18) between Workspace and Money, holding Messaging and the new Meetings row; the `/meetings` screen behind that row lists what is live, ahead and recently ended, over a cursor-paged `GET /api/v1/meetings`. Messaging keeps its stored id so a member's stars survive the move.

**The browser's half of an audio call.** The client takes the room's medium at `join` and captures the microphone ALONE in a call — a camera captured and muted still lights the device's own indicator, and the room would refuse the picture anyway — so it offers one track, declines a screen share before the picker is ever opened, and draws each participant as their initials over an audio element instead of a dark video one. The control bar drops the two controls a call cannot honour rather than grey them, the entry window offers **Start Meeting** and **Start Call** side by side under the one host key, and Join, the Meetings page's row glyphs and the header all read the medium off the record.

title: The editor container shows four threads for one round, to see the audit's hardware warning clear
entry: **The editor container is `standard-4` for one round, to see the audit's hardware warning clear.** coolwsd sets that warning whenever the kernel shows it fewer than four threads; `per_document.max_concurrency` cannot clear it, since it is only ever clamped down to the thread count, and the audit's only override (`disable_server_audit`) switches the whole audit off. Four vCPUs is the smallest instance that shows four threads, so this is the experiment; the owner's standing ruling is the `standard-1` price, and the container returns there once the audit is read. `docs/operating-costs.md` carries the figures.

title: Every number the firm issues is drawn from one register, and the firm shapes each one from Settings › Numbering
entry:
**Every number the firm issues is drawn from one register.** The segment-template scheme engine
moves out of `@magna-carta/matters` into `@magna-carta/sequence-numbering` beside the counter
mechanism it already held, under a static register of purposes (`purposes.ts`) naming what each
sequence is, when it is drawn, whether the firm shapes it and with which parts, and what renders
until it does. Conflicts checks and custody packets join as scheme-shaped purposes: a check draws
through the shared planner and its own counter tables instead of `MAX + 1` under a hard-coded
`CC-` prefix, defaulting to `CC2026-00001` restarting each year; a packet draws from the
`custody_packet` purpose with its old `CUS-00001` shape as the default, and custodian's dead
fixed-shape model is deleted. Invoice, time-entry and call numbers are registered with their fixed
shapes. `GET /api/v1/numbering-schemes` lists the register; `Settings › Practice › Numbering`
(formerly Matter Numbering, which redirects) shows one plate per sequence. Decision:
`docs/decisions/pending/every-number-the-firm-issues-is-drawn-from-one-register.md`.

title: Ask whether a browser session survives, rather than assuming it
entry:
**Whether a browser session survives between requests is now a question with an answer.** The safe
website viewer's capture reaches the rendering service through quick actions, which are one request
in and one answer out — the browser that served a capture is gone before the next starts. Interactive
browsing needs the opposite, and that is a different API against the same binding
(`@cloudflare/puppeteer`, added to the catalogue at 1.4.0, Apache-2.0) that nothing in this
repository had ever exercised.

`POST /api/v1/safe-browse/session-probe` exercises it once and reports each step: read the account's
limits and open sessions, launch, navigate, disconnect leaving the session alive, reconnect to the
same session id, navigate again, attach a CDP session and enable `Page`. Two facts decide what can
be built — `sessionReused`, without which every navigation pays a cold browser and carries no
cookies, and `cdpAttached`, without which pixel streaming is ruled out whatever else works.

It is gated on `tools:safeBrowse` and audited, because each run acquires a real session and is billed
for the time it is held; the browser is closed in a `finally` whatever happens, and `sessionsBefore`
reports what was already open so a leak shows up rather than staying invisible.

**It navigates only to a constant held in its own file, and that is a constraint rather than an
unfinished edge.** A route that drives a real browser to a caller's address is the SSRF surface the
whole safe-browse subsystem is built to contain, and the guard that contains it belongs on an
interactive route when there is one — not bolted onto a diagnostic. This probe answers a question
about the platform and must never be extended into a browsing endpoint.

The shape is a direct answer to the preceding round, which spent weeks attributing every failed
capture to an account entitlement that had been working the whole time. Make the unknown answerable
before building on it.

title: The editor image bind-mounts its kit jail, and the capabilities experiment is recorded as a success
entry: **The editor image no longer switches off `mount_jail_tree`, and the capabilities experiment is recorded as a success.** The owner's deploy of 2026-09-19 showed the runtime jails the kit with `security.capabilities` at its default (the audit reports each document as securely contained), which makes a mount namespace of the kit's own likely, and in that namespace the bind mount the fast path needs is permitted. coolwsd tests the mount at startup and falls back to copying if it fails, so the worst outcome is the audit's "cannot bind-mount" line rather than an outage; the Dockerfile's note carries the one-line revert.

title: The editor image tries to jail its kit: security.capabilities back at the image's default
entry: **The editor image no longer switches off `security.capabilities`.** An experiment the owner asked for on 2026-09-19 to clear the server audit's "Documents are not effectively contained" line: with the setting at its default, coolwsd first tries a user and mount namespace for the kit, and failing that needs the file capabilities the image sets on coolforkit. The Dockerfile's note carries the two outcomes to read after the deploy and the one-line revert (`--o:security.capabilities=false` back into `extra_params`) if no document opens.

title: Every document records its changes under a firm policy; the opening panel tells the open as it happens; the way back leads the editor's bar
entry:
**The firm's editing policy: every document opened in the browser editor records its changes.** One
setting (`editing.record_changes`, on by default, `@magna-carta/file-manager/editing-policy-settings`)
behind a new permission (`firm:manageEditingPolicy`, seeded to Owner/Admin), a GET/PATCH route at
`/api/v1/firm/editing-policy` on the scan-policy pattern (audited, one idempotent batch), and a page
at Settings · Documents · Editing over the shared server-backed draft. The WOPI host reads the policy
on every CheckFileInfo and answers `DisableChangeTrackingRecord: false` while it is on — the
property is tri-state on the editor's side and an explicit false forces recording ON with the control
withheld — and omits it when off, which is the firm stepping back rather than forbidding. The launch
carries `recordsChanges`, and the editor screen sends `.uno:ShowTrackedChanges` false once the
document is showing, so the marks are recorded and not shown. The seam it leaves behind: the stored
document keeps every mark, and accepting them on every copy that leaves the platform is the
conversion container's work, not built yet.

**The document-opening panel streams the open instead of ticking boxes.** `openFeed` in `apps/web/src/lib/documents/editor-open-progress.ts` turns the stage marks into lines as they happen (a finished stage is one past-tense line with its second; the stage under way says what it is doing and why it takes the time); `openPace` fills a `Progress` bar over `TYPICAL_OPEN_MILLISECONDS` (30 s, the owner's own opens) with the usual time said beside it, never a fraction of the stages; Retry now waits for `RETRY_AFTER_MILLISECONDS` (45 s) rather than the loading region's 15 s; the full ProgressSteps sequence and the failure rows sit behind a Show details control, shown unasked once the open has stopped. The "N seconds so far" line is gone. The editor container moves from `standard-1` to `standard-2` (one vCPU, 6 GiB) on the owner's ruling after the editor's hardware warning; `docs/operating-costs.md` carries the new figure.

**The back-to-matter button sits first on the editor's bar, carries the matter's number, and takes the editor's icon colour.** The editor appends a host's buttons after its own and shows the icon as given (`insertBefore` is honoured only by its classic toolbar), so the edit worker now serves the platform's stylesheet on the editor's origin (`apps/edit-worker/src/editor-stylesheet.ts`, at `/magna-carta/editor.css`, linked into the page's head as it streams through, under the page's own `style-src 'self'`): the shortcuts row is laid out as a flex line with the host's cell ordered first, and the icon is inverted under the editor's dark theme. `backToMatterButton` takes the matter's number as the button's word, threaded from the edit page's matter record; a matter without one reads "Matter".

title: The event form is four tabs, a staff member is an owner, and a zone reads as one line
entry:
**The event form is four tabs, a staff member is an owner, and a zone reads as one line.** The
owner's round of 2026-09-18 on `apps/web/src/lib/calendar`. `record-event-dialog.svelte` renders
Details, When, Where and Who over `EVENT_FORM_TABS` in `event-draft.ts`; its Belongs to is the
product's one closed-choice field with three owners, and the staff arm is `withMemberListed` — a
firm event with the people-listed audience and that member first. The second field on that line is
one slot, so the choice no longer reflows the form. `readsAsAllDay` / `asAllDay` are the All Day
switch's reading. The design system's `inAllDayBand` (`day-axis.ts`) sends a run of days to the
band above the hours; `day-segments.ts` no longer cuts a span into per-day pieces, which is what
drew a trial across every hour and gave each piece an id no press could open. `formatTimeZone` and
`describeTimeZone` join the display vocabulary (`formatters/instant.ts`) as the one line every zone
reads as, on the record's day; `time-zone-options.ts` orders the rest west to east and searches a
haystack, and `formatWallClock` prints the code beside an hour. `location-picker.svelte` offers the
offices with their addresses (the calendar context reads `listOffices` whole), the rooms, and the
directory's organizations through `directoryPickerSearch`. `participantsBySource` bundles the
chips. `calendar-menu.svelte` is the rail's selection as a dropdown, drawn by `CalendarView` on
`calendarMenu` for the day pane. Every self-clearing picker passes `allowDeselect={false}`, which
is what emptied the matter field on a re-pick. `DISCARD_SENTENCE` is gone from the action dialog.
The design system's `Tooltip.Provider` defaults `ignoreNonKeyboardFocus` on, so the focus a
closing popover hands back to the header's button no longer opens its tooltip.

title: The viewer is shipped, because a capture came back
entry:
**The safe website viewer is `shipped`, because a capture came back.** The feature-ledger node
stayed `partial` through the merge that repaired the render, on the rule that a capability's status
follows evidence rather than a deploy; the first successful capture against the deployed service
arrived on 2026-09-18 and the node follows it. Its `notes` no longer claim the page answers every
capture with a renderer-unavailable state, which stopped being true with that merge.

**The Browser Rendering entry in the deploy queue closes, and not the way it was written.** It had
stood open for weeks as the suspected cause of every failed capture — the one dependency no session
could verify from the repository. The entitlement had been serving the whole time. The captures were
failing on a wait for `networkidle2` that a page holding a socket never reaches, which the service
answered 422 and the route reported as a capacity outage.

The entry is closed with that correction rather than a tick, because the shape of the mistake is
what the file invites: an item naming something no session can check attracts any failure that might
plausibly be it, and the attribution is never re-tested. The renderer's own refusals were being
collapsed into a single sentence and never logged, so for weeks there was nothing to read. Make a
failure readable before blaming an open entry for it.

title: The capture waits for something every page reaches, and an Error ID says where it came from
entry:
**An Error ID says when and where it came from.** Its body carries 9 base36 milliseconds since the
epoch, a 3-character service code and 9 base62 random characters; `describeErrorId` in
`@magna-carta/telemetry/ids` reads it back. Both facts are on the log record already, and being on
the record is no help while the record is the thing being searched for: a member quotes an id days
later, and whoever reads it has to choose a Worker and judge whether retention still holds the
window before the search can start.

**The fields are packed INTO the existing 21-character body, never appended.** That body's shape is
pinned in three places that know nothing about the telemetry package — the per-entity identifier
validators, the `pattern` emitted for every identifier field in the OpenAPI document, and the
scrubber's whole-handle exemption. The last is the sharp one: a handle the scrubber stops
recognising is rewritten to `[scrubbed]` on the way out, destroying the very Error ID a failure is
keyed by. Keeping the budget means every previously minted id stays well-formed and no contract
moves. The random part drops from ~126 bits to ~53, which is ample for a correlation handle that
grants nothing and addresses no record, and would not be acceptable for a handle that names one.

A 9-character timestamp rather than 8 because 8 runs out in 2059 and would have truncated silently
into a confidently wrong date; the test that pins both ends of the range is what found it. A Worker
announces itself once through `setServiceIdentity`, from the module its events pass through rather
than its entrypoint, which is held to a startup CPU budget the telemetry import would spend. A
Worker that never announces mints `unk`.

**And one failure now mints one Error ID.** `logOperationFailed` returns the id it minted. A caller
that had to show the member an id used to mint its own and call this too, which minted a second —
so the record's `errorId` field named a failure nobody held, and the member's id survived only if
the caller had buried it in the message. A support search against the field found nothing, which is
the one thing that field exists to make possible.

**The capture waits for something every page reaches.** The first refusal the safe website viewer
could actually read said `http=422, code=6004` — which the rendering service documents as being
unable to complete the action because of an issue with the site, most often a timeout. The cause was
ours: the snapshot asked the browser to wait for `networkidle2` before shooting, and a page holding
a socket, a poll or an analytics beacon never reaches two-connections-idle, so the wait ran to its
own 45-second limit and the service gave up. Every capture against a live commercial page failed
that way, and the answer on screen blamed capacity. The capture now waits for `load`, a condition
every page reaches, and the bounded settle afterwards is what covers the painting that idle was
there to wait for.

A page that still will not finish gets a second attempt with everything expensive turned off — no
lazy-load sweep, the earliest ready signal, the first viewport only. A worse screenshot is worth
more than none on a surface whose whole purpose is looking at pages chosen for being suspect. Only
a page failure earns that retry: a capacity shortage and a configuration refusal fail identically
on a second ask, so retrying either would spend a second render to learn nothing.

A failed render is now its own answer (`page-render-failed`, HTTP 422) rather than borrowing one
that fits it badly. It is not the capacity 502, which invites a retry the server has already made,
and it is not the 500, which hands the member an Error ID for a page that is merely slow.

title: Documents is the firm's template library, and a template goes onto several matters at once
entry:
**The Documents destination ships, as the firm's template library.** The sidebar row had been a Soon stub since the rail was drawn; behind it now is `/documents`, the firm-level catalogue the matter's Files page has been building single documents from since slice 2·6·1 landed the routes — on the platform's one table (`apps/web/src/lib/templates/template-columns.ts`), read through the generated client and warmed from the route's load. Standing is derived rather than served: the listing carries a status word and a current-version handle, and only the pair says whether a template can be built from today (ready · being checked · archived), which is the rule the matter's picker already applied silently.

**A template is registered from the browser** (`register-template.ts`): presign, PUT to storage, register — the kind read off the file rather than asked for, because the signed URL covers the content type. The registration report is rendered as findings, so a Word merge field left unconverted, a legacy form field nothing binds, or a box on a form nothing fills is said out loud at the moment somebody can still do something about it.

**One template goes onto several matters at once** (`add-to-matters.ts`). An assembly stays what it is on the server — one job on one matter, behind that matter's own wall — and adding to five matters is five jobs, each under its own idempotency key, each polled to its own standing, none of them stopped by another's refusal. A document that landed with blanks is its own standing rather than "landed": it is on the matter and it needs a person's eye before it goes anywhere.

Archive is offered to a member holding `templates:manage`. The field inspector and authoring in the browser remain unbuilt.

title: The opening wait is one panel, the way back is on the editor's bar, every save is a version, and history says who was there
entry:
**Every save in the browser editor is a version, history folds the autosaves, and each version says who was in the document.**

A version was cut only when a session ended, and later only on the member's own save and the exit save; the editor's autosave every few minutes kept the working copy and nothing else. The owner's ruling is that the timeline of every state is the point, and that too many rows is a folding problem: every save with changed bytes is a version now, autosaves included, and the version carries what kind of save cut it (`save_kind`: the member's own, the autosave, the exit save, or the idle reap). History shows the named saves and folds the autosaves behind one line that says how many there are, opened with a click.

Each version cut from the working copy also records everyone with a view open at that moment (`file_version_participant`), so history reads "Ana · with Trevor, Mira" rather than the one name whose save happened to cut it. Names are read off the member roster when history is read, so a renamed member reads under their current name and a departed one keeps their identifier.

One per-firm migration: the column and the table. Design: `docs/specs/2026-09-17-document-history-and-attribution-design.md`, layers one and two.

**The editor's corner no longer carries its vendor's logo.**

The editor hides its logo when a hidden field on its page reads `none`, and the community build of the image leaves that field empty with no setting to fill it. The worker in front of the container now fills it, rewriting that one attribute as the page streams through; nothing is injected, because the page's own policy allows no inline style or script, and an upgrade is handed back untouched as before.

**The document's opening wait is one centered panel over the frame, and the way back to the matter is a button on the editor's own bar.**

The staged wait sat above the frame, the "taking longer" sentence and its Retry arrived above that at fifteen seconds, and when the editor came up the panel went away and the frame moved up into its place: three reflows on a screen a member was staring at. The panel now sits over the frame, centered, with the frame beneath it at its final size from the start; the sentence, the Retry and a failure all appear inside the same panel, which grows downward only. Time is written out ("12 seconds so far"), never abbreviated.

With the editor the whole screen, the way back is a button the editor draws for us: **Matter**, on the editor's shortcuts bar, inserted through its message protocol and labelled with the matter it returns to. The editor's own Close is routed to the same exit. Both ask the editor to save first and leave when it says the save is done, or after three seconds if it does not; the editor saves on its own when the last view drops, so the wait protects the member's time, not their work.

Three corrections from the editor's own integration guide, now that it could be read: a save's answer carries `LastModifiedTime` as the JSON body the editor reads (an empty body was logged as invalid and left its change detection off); `CheckFileInfo` names the member (`UserFriendlyName`), so co-authors see a name rather than an unknown user with an identifier; and the frame allows full screen, which a slideshow needs. In the image, the kit's jail is set up by copying rather than by a bind-mount the container cannot make.

title: A renderer refusal says which refusal it was
entry:
**A renderer refusal says which refusal it was.** The safe website viewer signalled every structured
refusal from Cloudflare Browser Rendering by throwing one sentence containing the words "capacity"
and "limit", and both routes then decided the response by matching that sentence with `includes`.
Every distinguishable fault therefore collapsed into the same answer: an account without the
entitlement, a credential lacking the permission and a rejected parameter all reached the member as
a 502 saying the service was at capacity and to try again shortly. The service states its reason in
an `errors` array, and the renderer discarded it — reading only `success`, `result` and `meta` —
before anything could act on it.

The refusal now travels as `RendererFailure` (`packages/safe-browse/src/renderer-failure.ts`),
carrying the service's HTTP status and error code and, deliberately, nothing else: the upstream
message can quote the suspect URL back, so a failure that cannot hold the target cannot leak it
whatever a caller later logs. A status the service documents as momentary (408, 429, 5xx) stays the
transient 502; every other refusal describes how this worker is calling the service, which waiting
cannot fix, so it reaches the standard pipeline as a 500 with an Error ID to quote. Both paths now
log — the transient one answered and wrote nothing before, which is why the first live failure left
no trace at all. A non-2xx and an unparseable body are refusals too, rather than a `SyntaxError`
surfacing as an unexplained server fault.

title: The work canvas lays its children out, so a full-height screen shrinks under the platform notice
entry: **The work canvas lays its children out as a column, so a full-height screen shrinks under the platform notice.** `<main>` in `app-shell.svelte` is `flex flex-col`; `NavigationLayout`'s root is `min-h-0 shrink`. A two-sided screen sized itself to the whole canvas as a block child and kept that height whatever stood above it, so the platform notice pushed it past the bottom edge and the canvas grew a third scrollbar. The page-inset lint reads the canvas's class list, so its inert-grow rule retires itself on the same change. `personInitials` moves from the time sheet's column helpers to the design system's name formatters beside `personName`, which is the one home the account corner and the time ledger now share.

title: The owner's rounds of 2026-09-17 and 18: the settings column folds, the Directory searches its own table, one panel in the top bar, tables before rows, and the calendar on a laptop
entry:
**The owner's round of 2026-09-17, in five parts.** The favourite star in every screen header no longer announces itself pressed (`favorite-control.svelte`): the ghost button recipe rings a pressed control with an accent hairline, which drew a box around a glyph that already carries the state by filling. The settings column folds by band and by group through a new `NavigationLayout.Group` part (`packages/design-system/.../navigation-layout/`), remembered per browser as departures from everything-open (`settings-navigation-folds.svelte.ts`), never folding away the page the reader is on; `NavigationLayout` caps its height against the canvas it sits in instead of guessing from the viewport, and the conflicts settings page is on `SettingsScrollRegion` like the other twenty-three. The Directory searches its own table: `GET /api/v1/directory/entities` takes `search`, answers with listing rows in the firm's relevance order and says when the answer is capped, and matching matters ride the same grid as rows of kind Matter while a query is live; the separate hit table is gone. A fourth rule in `lint:workspace-search`, `second-results-surface`, refuses a Workspace screen that draws one table under the query and another under the else. The calendar fits a laptop: one scroll region under the action row (the agenda is its own), the month sized by a cell minimum that fills its column, and a toolbar that fits one line by measure rather than wrapping — the controls stay over the grid, as the owner ruled in the same breath as naming the escape.
The next morning's corrections ride the same branch: `ScreenSearch` no longer takes a placeholder, so every screen's search field reads the one word "Search" (twenty-three per-screen hints struck). The office editor launch form now carries `ui_defaults=UIMode=tabbed`, so Collabora opens in its tabbed interface with the font and paragraph controls on the Home tab instead of behind the Format menu. The top bar holds one open panel at a time: `TopBar.Root` declares an overlay band (`packages/design-system/src/lib/internal/overlay-band.svelte.ts`) that every popover, menu and dialog seated in it joins, because a hover label counts as a dismissible layer in Bits UI and could keep a neighbour's panel from closing; the account menu is click-only and shows the member's name and firm from the cached session bootstrap. In the file manager, folders form their own run above the files in every view under every column sort (`orderFolderRowsFirst` on the grid's `orderRows` seam; ledger row L59).

**Where a data table will hold the rows, the table renders first.** The owner's ruling of
2026-09-18, on the Downloads and Uploads registers: "downloads and upload pages should show the
table data would populate in, even if there is no data. i want this as a lint and standard rule,
that data tables will still appear before data is in the area. this prepares users for the proper
shape." The header row now stands from the first paint and the words about the emptiness live in
the table's own empty body, under it.

`DataTable.EmptyRow` is the new part that carries them for a hand-composed table: one row, one cell
spanning every column, one line in the table's muted register, styled by the same recipe as the
grid's own empty state and marked `data-placeholder` so it takes none of a row's treatment. Surfaces
built on `DataTable.Grid` needed no part — the grid already draws its header over its own empty body
and says "No Results" there — only the gate in front of it removed.

The fitness function gained a third rule, `table-behind-absence`
(`tooling/lint-structured-empty/`), which reads a Svelte file's markup tree for a data table gated
behind the absence of its own rows: a conditional whose absence branch renders the product's one
`EmptyState` where its other branch renders the table, and the same arrangement one layer in, where
a region is handed an `emptyState` snippet that replaces the table it would otherwise render. It
follows the table through any depth of snippet, and it deliberately leaves a refusal and a failure
alone — a member who may not see the table, and a read that broke, are not tables waiting to fill.
The inline `<!-- structured-empty-allow: <why> -->` works for it as for the other two.

What it found, and what changed: Downloads, Uploads, the directory record's names, categories,
matters, relationships and near-matches panes, the matter calendar's deadlines and events, an
event's bookings, the matter activity register, and the file inspector's versions and checks.

title: A text column's filter offers the column's values, and a date filter's calendar stays in the menu
entry: **A text column's grid filter is the set of its values, and a date filter's calendar stays inside the column's menu.** `gridColumnFilterKind` now defaults a text column to `set`; the contains box survives only for a declared prose column (the time and fee ledgers' Description). The set filter's one select control acts on the choices listed once the narrow field is in play (`facetSelectionAfterToggleValues`). The design system's submenu wrappers keep focus in a popover, select or combobox list as focus inside the field (`context-menu/menu-field-layer.ts`), which needed `patches/bits-ui@2.18.1.patch` to also wrap the focus-outside event so `preventDefault()` is honoured — a focus event is not cancelable, so Bits' documented route was a no-op. The file manager's Name, From, To and File or Folder, the upload's Name and the conflict hit's Party move to the set.

title: Claude Docs is assessed against the editor we ship, local-first editing is declined on the record, and the editor container loses its instance cap
entry:
The document editor's container class no longer carries `max_instances: 10`.

Ten was the number of documents the whole fleet could have open at once, across every firm, and the eleventh open would have failed at the container stage of the staged-open screen with nothing to say why. A fixed per-class cap is a cliff a growing fleet walks off; the bound is now the account's concurrent-instance limit, as it already is for six of the eight container workers here. The Host-label check in `apps/edit-worker/src/document-routing.ts` is what keeps an invented label from booting a container, and it is unchanged.

The size comment beside it is corrected. It named a "custom ~2.5 GiB instance" as the target, which the platform cannot configure — a custom type needs at least 1 vCPU and 3 GiB per vCPU — and it quoted a 1.16 GiB idle floor for which no measurement was ever recorded. The comment now says what is and is not known, and points at the sizing method in `docs/research/2026-09-18-local-first-document-editing.md`.

title: The file icon draws what the name claims; the analysis says whether it holds
entry:
**The file icon resolves from the name first; the type-mismatch finding grades in the icon's own
vocabulary.** `resolveFileCategory` in the design system's file-icon module reads the extension
before the sniffed content type, and an unrecognized extension resolves to `unknown` rather than
falling through to the bytes. A bytes-first sibling, `resolveFileContentCategory`, serves handling
decisions (`editable-documents.ts` keeps opening a Word document renamed `.txt` in the Word editor).
`file-analysis.ts` drops its ten-entry extension-to-MIME list and compares `claimedFileCategory`
against `sniffedFileCategory` at the level of kind: an unrecognized extension over a read sniff is a
mismatch, no extension is no claim, a sniff with no known kind is no reading. Rulings round R25.

title: Every download registers, and Downloads becomes a register
entry:
**Downloads is a register on the platform's one table.**

A fixed list of seven columns served a shelf that held one kind of thing. It holds five now — an export, a bundle, a converted file, a discovery production, a file taken off a matter — and they answer different questions, so the columns are declared (`apps/web/src/lib/export/download-columns.ts`) and the reader chooses: sort, per-column filters, show and hide, reorder, pin, and a layout that survives the visit. Type and Standing declare their whole vocabularies rather than reading them off the rows in hand, so a member with no conversions loaded this week is not told the register cannot hold one.

**Standing is the column the screen could not do without.** Now that the row outlives the bytes, "is this still here" stopped being answerable from the other columns: Available, Preparing, On the matter, and Record only are four different answers to "can I have it again", and the Download control is offered from the same reading.

**The read is paged and the search is the server's.** `GET /api/v1/downloads` answers the house `{ data, nextCursor }` envelope and takes a `search` that narrows the whole register — the register has no bound now, so filtering the rows a client happens to hold would answer confidently about a fraction of it. Taking several at once routes by kind rather than by "artifact or not": snapshots render into one archive, a matter file and a stored artifact each open on their own, and a record that never held bytes is reported as short rather than silently missing from the zip.

**The download register admits every download, and the row outlives the bytes.**

`download_item` was built as a shelf of what the platform MADE you, and only exports were ever written to it — `bundle` and `conversion` were named in its vocabulary from the start with no client able to create one, and a file downloaded from a matter had nowhere to go at all. So "I downloaded something and it did not appear in Downloads" was the correct behaviour, which is the definition of a design that needs changing.

One reviewed rebuild widens it. `producer` gains `file`; `kind` gains `reference` and `record`; `object_key` and `expires_at` become nullable, tied to the kind by CHECKs. `download_item` is a LEAF — nothing in the schema references it — so this is the `invoice_wip_claim` shape rather than the parent rebuild the repository forbids, and the audit is written out in the migration's own `-- contract:` header.

**`reference` is a safety boundary, not a vocabulary.** An artifact fetch presigns the stored object key with no further check, which is right for a frozen bundle the member already had and wrong for a live matter file: a member screened off a matter afterwards would keep a working handle to its files. A reference carries no key — the CHECK makes that unrepresentable rather than remembered — and the fetch hands back this platform's own `/api/v1/files/{id}/download` address, so the matter capability check runs again at the moment they ask. **`record`** is the register being complete without lying: a bundle streamed inline assembled its bytes for one response and never retained them, and filing those as an artifact would report "expired" for something that was never stored.

**Retention splits.** The bytes are privileged content in a second place and keep the seven-day rule; the row is a title, a producer and two instants, and is kept. The sweep marks `expired` and takes the object where it used to delete both, and the read it drives excludes what it has already marked so that marking terminates. The shelf read is paged for the first time, on the `(created_at, id)` pair the index already leads on — its old comment reasoned that a whole read was safe because the shelf was short-lived by construction, and keeping rows takes that premise away.

title: The security audit runs weekly, and a pull request asks whether its angle was run
entry: The whole-repo security audit is now scheduled: a weekly Claude Code Routine (`MC - Security Audit`, Wednesdays 13:00 UTC, fresh session per firing) runs the vendored security-audit skill in full audit mode over `main`, opens one `remediate-` pull request per confirmed finding with a regression verifier, and reports needs-validation leads by notification. Audit artifacts never enter the repository. The canonical configuration lives beside the audit policy in `docs/conventions/testing.md`, the `maintenance-agents.security` roadmap node moves to partial, and the pull request template gains a row asking whether the security angle was run against the companion files the change reaches.

title: The document open is staged, the editor is the whole screen, every office format opens, and saving is not refused
entry:
**Saving in the editor was refused every time, because the host required a lock it never told the editor to take.**

The editor takes a lock on a document only when the host's CheckFileInfo answer says it supports locks. Ours never said so, so the editor never locked; and the host refused any save made without a held lock, answering a conflict, which the editor showed as the document having been changed by another user. The answer now advertises the lock contract it enforces (`SupportsLocks`, `SupportsUpdate`), and states `IsAdminUser` so the editor's server audit stops reporting it missing.

With locks in use, a second defect was waiting behind the first: one container serves a document, and a container that stops without unlocking left its lock in the session record, so the next instance's lock was refused and the document read as held by another editor. A plain lock request carrying a different value is now the successor taking over; releasing or refreshing a lock still requires the held value, so an old instance cannot release a successor's.

Also in the image: the editor's own "what's new" dialog no longer opens on every first open of a document. It remembers having been seen in the browser's storage for the editor's origin, and every document here is its own origin. Help › What's New still opens it; whether the editor was updated is the platform's version report to say.

**Spreadsheets, presentations and drawings open in the browser editor, and one register says how every kind of file opens.**

Only word-processing documents opened in the editor. The editor is Collabora Online, and the formats it opens are the ones its own discovery document lists for Writer, Calc, Impress and Draw; those lists are now the platform's, so a spreadsheet, a presentation or a drawing opens the way a document does, older formats included (WordPerfect, Lotus 1-2-3, Keynote, Pages, Numbers, Visio). A legacy format the ingest gate has no signature for is known by its extension, which is what the editor decides by too.

Which formats take which way is one register (`apps/web/src/lib/documents/file-type-register.ts`): the file manager decides the one Open gesture from it, and **Settings › Documents › Opening Files** renders it, so what a member reads there is what the product does. The page is a routing table with nothing to change yet — every family opens one way — built so that when a family gains a second way of opening, the choice is made there. Guide: `docs/user/admin/opening-files.md`.

**While a document is open, the editor is the whole screen.**

The edit screen drew the app's rail, the top bar, and a header naming the document over the editor, and the editor had what was left. The owner's direction is that the editor is the only thing on the screen: the page declares that it declines the shell, the app layout draws no rail and no top bar for it, and the page draws no header. A failure, a withheld file and a format with no editor keep the shell, because each of those is a message that needs its way back around it. What a member does on the platform from inside the document — save and close, the way back to the matter — will be the editor's own controls, added to its toolbar through its message protocol; until then, the way back is the browser's.

**Opening a document in the editor names each stage as it happens, and a stall names the stage it stopped at.**

Opening a document is a chain: the editing session is opened, the editor's container starts, the editor page loads, the editor asks the host about the document, fetches its contents, and shows it. The screen showed one sentence for up to ninety seconds and then a failure that could not say which link had broken — and every failure this path has had was in a different link. The wait is now a staged list that advances as each stage completes, with the time elapsed beside it.

The two stages the screen cannot see from the browser — the editor asking the host about the document, and fetching its contents — are the ones that failed most, because they happen inside the container. The host now records each of the editor's calls against the member's open (which call, what it was answered, and the Error ID where it was refused), and the screen reads that record while it waits. So a stall says "the editor came up but never asked the host about the document", or "the host refused the editor's request for the document's contents (answered 404)" with the Error ID, and the failure details list every stage with when it was reached, as one block a member can copy into a report.

title: The vendored security-audit skill catches up with upstream, and the formatter learns to leave it alone
entry:
The vendored `security-audit` skill (`.claude/skills/security-audit/`, Cloudflare, MIT) is refreshed to upstream commit `c1c8a8c` of 2026-09-14. The copy landed on 2026-09-11 was already three months behind: it carried the seven original files and none of the domain companions upstream had added since July.

What arrives: a coverage ledger (`coverage-ledger.json`, with its own validator and test suite) so a run records what it checked, not only what it found; a third verdict, `needs_validation`, for a lead with an exact unresolved fact and no severity, so a blocked lead is no longer either inflated to confirmed or dropped; a guidance mode, so loading the skill for a security question no longer starts the six-phase audit or writes files; an execution-safety rule that runs target code only inside an OS-enforced sandbox and otherwise keeps the lead as needs-validation; and ten domain hunting files, of which the tenant-isolation, cloud-and-deployment, supply-chain, resource-exhaustion, and AI-and-LLM ones map onto this platform directly. `VENDORED.md` in the skill directory records the pinned commit and the refresh procedure; the directory joins the formatter's ignore list in `vite.config.ts`, because upstream owns the bytes and because the formatter corrupts one of its files on a second pass; and the security angle of the 7-angle review in `docs/conventions/testing.md` now names the companion files a slice picks from.

title: A participant's role is offered, not asked for blind
entry:
**The event participant's role is the product's dropdown-with-add instead of a bare text box.** `apps/web/src/lib/calendar/participant-role-field.svelte` offers `PARTICIPANT_ROLE_OPTIONS` (eighteen roles, alphabetical, in `calendar-vocabulary.ts`) and ends the list in `Combobox.AddOption`, so a role the list has never heard of is still typed and kept — the column stays free text, which the per-firm schema rules deliberately because the vocabulary is jurisdiction-specific and nothing downstream reads it.

The standing rule under _Data entry_ in `docs/conventions/design-corrections.md` already decided the control ("a vocabulary that is not closed but is not free either is the product's dropdown-with-add … the same control in every such field"); the location field on the same form and the matter-party role already had it, and this field was the one that had not been carried over. A closed dropdown was considered and rejected: the roles a practice needs do not close, and a fixed list missing one makes somebody pick a wrong-but-adjacent role, which corrupts the consistency the list existed for and does it invisibly.

`settledParticipantRole` collapses a typed role onto an offered spelling in any casing, so "court reporter" no longer founds a second role beside "Court reporter"; anything unlisted is kept exactly as typed, trimmed. The field's name stays "Role" rather than the clearer "Attending as" because `AddOption` reads the name into a row that says `Add <name>`. Pinned by `apps/web/test/calendar-participant-roles.test.ts`.

title: The WOPI handler is registered where the container proxy reads it
entry:
**The editor's container was refusing its own WOPI callback, because the handler for it was declared where the runtime could see it and not where the proxy reads it.**

With the frame allowed, the socket connected and the host trusted, coolwsd's first call to the WOPI host — `CheckFileInfo`, the call that decides whether a document opens at all — came back 520, and the container log named it: `WOPI::CheckFileInfo returned 520 (Unknown) Server Error`, then `CheckFileInfo failed … State::Fail`, and the editing session was dropped. 520 is `@cloudflare/containers`' own "Origin is disallowed" answer, the one it gives a host it intercepted but found no handler for.

The handler was there. `DocumentEditorContainer` declared it as `static outboundByHost = { … }`, the shape the library's README shows. But `Container` declares `outboundByHost` as a static accessor pair whose setter files the handlers in a module-level registry keyed by class name, and that registry is what `ContainerProxy` reads when the intercepted request arrives. Under the class-field semantics this repository compiles to (ES2022), a static field is a definition, not an assignment: it creates an own property on the subclass that shadows the inherited setter, which never runs. The two halves of the library then disagreed. The half that decides which hosts to intercept reads the property, so the WOPI host was intercepted; the half that dispatches reads the registry, found nothing, and refused.

The handler is now registered by assignment in a static block, which reaches the inherited setter. The proof runs the library's real dispatch: `test/document-editor-container.test.ts` builds the `ContainerProxy` the runtime would build for this class and sends it coolwsd's callback, which now reaches the app worker, while every other host is still refused. Against the shipped class the same test answers 520 — the production failure, reproduced. To run it, the edit worker's suite inlines the library and answers `cloudflare:workers` with a two-class stub; the Container class had been kept out of the suite until now, and this is the one test that needs it.

title: A date that is today and selected can be read again
entry:
**A day that was both today and the selected day rendered as its own foreground colour on no background at all.** `date-range-picker.css` declared its band states as bare `.mc-calendar-day[...]` selectors, and `components.css` imports it after `calendar.css` — so at equal specificity and later source order, the range picker's `[data-today] { background-color: transparent }` beat the plain calendar's `[data-selected]` fill on every calendar in the product, while selection's near-white foreground survived. White text, white surface. The range picker's rules are now scoped to a `.mc-date-range-calendar` class the popover carries, and `calendar.css` marks today with an inset hairline ring and a heavier numeral rather than a fill, so today and selection compose instead of one erasing the other.
