The file list is the product's one grid, so it sorts by name, type, size and arrival, filters per column, hides and reorders columns, and carries the count and the selection in its own footer — the same behaviours the matter's ledgers have. The list itself takes a drop, with nothing drawn for it until a drag is over it; each row has its own menu; and one control shows or hides the file beside its readings, whichever capability is open.

The capability set is a registry of self-contained modules: adding one is a module and a line in an array, and the Overview is contributed by the modules rather than written by hand, so the synthesis cannot fall behind the set. The modules carry no components — a panel reaches bits-ui through the design system, and golden rule 2 keeps that inside the design system strictly enough that a registry carrying one could not be loaded by a test at all.

title: A generated file gets a shelf, not a notification: the download register
entry:
The download register: a per-member shelf at `/downloads` of what the platform produced for that
member, held for seven days and downloadable again until it expires. It exists because the platform
had no durable record of a generated file at all — a bulk bundle is addressed by the content hash of
its selection and a conversion by its job id, both held only in a Durable Object and an R2 object, so
a member who closed the tab lost the artifact while its bytes sat in the bucket until the lifecycle
rule reaped them.

Routing completions through the notification feed was considered and **rejected on the owner's
ruling: notifications carry matter work, and a generated file is platform mechanics.** The two
surfaces stay separate in both directions — no producer raises a notification to say an artifact is
ready.

Two row kinds share one table because the member asks one question. A kept **artifact** points at
bytes that cannot be re-derived and re-downloads as a freshly minted presigned GET, so the browser's
own download manager keeps pause and resume; the register never proxies bytes. A kept **snapshot** is
an export, and stores the tabular DOCUMENT rather than a rendered file — one row serves every format,
and cells keep their number face so a re-rendered workbook still sums. New: `download_item` (per-firm,
member-scoped, journaled with its `downloads:shelf` seed to every default role), four routes under
`/api/v1/downloads`, and a retention sweep on the daily per-firm cron that takes the stored document
before the row. The export menu keeps every download it takes, in all six formats, including the three
the browser renders and the printer never sees.

title: The version panel says each thing once, and its gestures sit together
entry:
**The Build Versions panel stopped saying the same thing twice, and its two gestures moved into one cluster.** Five owner rulings from a deployed-site walk, recorded in [`docs/conventions/design-corrections.md`](docs/conventions/design-corrections.md):

- The standing **"This page / committed … · built …"** row duplicated `magna-carta-web`. That Worker serves the interface, so its commit and timestamps already are this page's, said once under a name someone can open in a dashboard. `showsPageBuildRow` in `apps/web/src/lib/versions/version-overlay-model.ts` keeps the line as a fallback rather than deleting it outright: signed out, a read that failed, or a web row that came back silent all leave nothing else able to state this build, and a panel reporting no version at all is the opposite of the point. While a first read is still in flight it stays away, so it cannot appear for a moment and then vanish when the answer lands.
- **"Services checked … ago"** sits under the header instead of beside the controls. Its length changes on a clock, and on the header row that motion pushed the Refresh button around while a reader was aiming at it.
- **Reload** is now a warning-tinted `rotate-cw` symbol beside Refresh, appearing only while the version poll has a newer bundle in hand. It reads as the answer to the chip's dot rather than as a second refresh, and the Update Available block keeps the badge and the sentence without a second copy of the gesture.
- The **Workers** beneath the leading pair fold behind a caret, remembered per browser on the shared persisted-preference primitive (`version-panel-preferences.svelte.ts`). It defaults to open, and a shut heading counts the Workers that came back without a version, so folding hides rows and never hides a fault: the fleet list is exhaustive precisely because an omission reads as health.
- **Copying a version** darkens the control for a second instead of growing a check beside the commit. The glyph widened the button on every press, and the width change read as the identifier itself changing.

title: The Docket's rulings land in the file manager: Fees tab, zip browsing, a history that says what changed
entry:
**Browse Inside a zip, and a file history that says what changed.** Two File Manager reads. `GET
/api/v1/files/{id}/archive-entries` (`files.archiveEntries`) lists a zip's entries by reading only
its central directory from R2 — ranged reads via a hand-rolled parser in
`packages/file-manager/src/zip-central-directory.ts` (EOCD scan, ZIP64 locator/record, capped
directory walk), never the archive's body, never extraction. The container is treated as hostile:
the directory read and the entry count are capped (the firm's `fileManager.archiveCaps.maxEntries`)
with `truncated: true` instead of a throw, traversal paths are skipped, and only "not a zip at all"
errors. A soft-deleted zip browses exactly like a live one — browsing restores nothing. Second, the
file-history writes now record their from/to facts as ids in audit metadata (`file.moved` /
`file.deleted` carry folder ids, `file.document_type_assigned` its type id, uploads their folder,
`file.restored` normalized to `toFolderId`), and `files.history` resolves them server-side into
`fromText`/`toText` — current folder path text ("Home" for the root, a fixed fallback for a folder
no longer on the matter), the document type's current name, version numbers. File names never ride
audit metadata (redact-by-default), so a rename's from/to stay honest nulls, as do rows written
before the facts were recorded.

**File Analysis is a plain file table, and the file manager's header holds still.** The strip above
the File Analysis table is gone entirely — the Safety column already filters, so a second row of
controls above the table said the same thing twice. The view's own acts moved to the footer beside
undo/redo: the door into the set-aside issues and the report download (the copy button is gone; the
download produces the same text). Browsing inside a zip likewise adds nothing above the table: the
archive's crumb, its badges, the extract seam, and the way out sit on the archive's own line just
above the footer, so entering and leaving an archive never moves the header and never costs the
footer a tool.

**The file manager now matches the owner's settled Docket design, and Fees stands beside Time and
Costs.** The work-in-progress fee ledger left the Billing tabs for its own matter section, and
Billing (the bill register) wears the Alpha mark instead of Soon. On the Files surface: the
breadcrumb and navigation controls sit directly above the file list rather than spanning the whole
surface, the counts footer is pinned to the bottom of the screen and tallies folders and files with
a select all/none toggle, the New control anchors the toolbar's far end, and the matter's status
seal moved beside the matter number in the masthead's top-left corner. Toolbar and footer controls
are quiet glyphs — no resting box, no grey plate behind a disabled undo/redo, an active toggle
reading through its glyph and a hairline — the columns control included; the file area's edges are
square; the pane dividers lost their grip handles; and both side panels sit on the sunken surface
so they read as panels. Collapsing or reopening a side panel now hands the space to the file list
alone instead of resizing the opposite panel. The folder tree's right-click grew the full file
menu — open, download, pin, rename, cut, paste, delete, colour and mark. Uploading no longer waits
on the destination question: files start uploading the moment they are picked (drag-and-drop onto
the list included), the Upload dialog shows each file's own progress while the destination —
Current Folder, Home, or Select Folder over the real folder tree — is chosen, and a failed upload
now names the stage it failed at and quotes the Error ID.

**The matter file manager's recovery and history reads exist as routes** — `GET
/api/v1/matters/{matterId}/files/deleted` lists a matter's soft-deleted files newest-deletion-first
(the deleter resolved from the audit trail, never a fabricated actor), `POST
/api/v1/files/{id}/restore` undeletes a file into the folder it came from, a chosen folder, or the
matter root when the original folder is gone, and `GET /api/v1/matters/{matterId}/file-history`
reads the matter's file activity trail straight off the per-firm audit log with names resolved at
read time. The upload policy also gains the Windows-declared zip aliases
(`application/x-zip-compressed`, `application/x-compressed`) beside `application/zip`, so a zip
uploaded from Windows clears initiate.

title: The export prints through the platform's one printer: Word and PDF land on the menu
entry:
The export menu gains the two document formats, rendered server-side through the platform's one
printer: `POST /api/v1/reports/exports` takes the tabular document the client already holds (wire
shape and bounds in the new `@magna-carta/export-document` package), composes a plain
word-processing package through document assembly's guarded writer (`compose/tabular.ts`, this
package's first table emitter — byte-reproducible, header rows repeating across pages, figure
columns right-aligned), and for PDF carries those bytes across the registry's one docx-to-pdf edge,
answering an honest 503 when the office-suite engine is unreachable rather than an Error ID. The
route rides the chokepoint under the new `reports:export` permission (seeded to Owner/Admin), and a
failed render surfaces as a toast carrying the server's own words — the design-system Toaster is
now mounted at the app root for it. Spec:
`docs/specs/2026-08-31-tabular-export-rendering-design.md`.

title: The sweep loads what scrolling would, and the viewer fits the monitor
entry:
**Full-page captures load what scrolling would, and the viewer fits the monitor.** Below-the-fold
images lazy-load on scroll, so a full-page screenshot without a scroll captured gray placeholders
under the first viewport: the snapshot call now injects a bounded scroll sweep (`addScriptTag`,
viewport steps to the bottom or thirty steps, whichever first, then back to the top) with the
settle timeout raised to cover the loads it triggers — bounded so an infinite-scroll feed cannot
hold a capture hostage. And the viewer's full-height column double-claimed the canvas: the page's
`h-full` took 100% of the canvas height on top of the Back-to-Tools row above it, so the frame's
bottom edge always sat below the fold and the screenshot's inner scrollbar with it. The tools
layout now owns the height column (nav row fixed, slot takes the remainder), so the viewer sizes
to the monitor exactly and normal-flow tool pages keep scrolling the canvas as before.

title: Deploy skew stops blaming the address, and the viewer fills the screen
entry:
**Deploy skew stops reading as "that address cannot be viewed".** The interface and the API ship
as separate Workers since this morning, so a freshly deployed page can meet an older API: the
viewer's new streaming route answered 404 there, and the problem guidance's default case blamed
the member's address for it — youtube.com, google, and 8.8.8.8 all "failed" identically. Three
fixes in the seam: a 404 from our own API now reads as "The service is mid-update" with refresh
guidance, never an input fault; `viewSafelyStaged` falls back to the non-streaming capture when
the streaming route is not deployed, so skew costs the narration, not the capture; and
`normalizeTarget` refuses a bare single label ("google") at the field with the inline hint — it
parses as a URL but names no public host, so it only bought a round trip to a refusal. Screen
side: the export menu's format rows carry the same file symbols the file manager uses for xlsx,
csv, and txt, and the viewer's Static/Live control joins into one segmented button whose halves
touch, active side filled.

title: Retire the firm-usage stream note
The stamp is the reader's clock, on two lines, with its zone named
entry:
The export generation stamp splits into two lines — the date, then the time on its own line — and
the time now names its zone (`12:57:56 PM PDT`), rendered from the reader's own clock via the two
shared helpers in `$lib/export/tabular-export.ts` that all four renderers now draw from. The stamp
was always browser-local; naming the zone is what makes that self-evident to whoever a file is
forwarded to. Verified by generating in a headless browser pinned to Pacific time on a UTC machine.

title: A workbook says when its figures were true, in either layout, under its own name
entry:
Three corrections to the Excel export on the owner's review: the menu now offers both layouts
(`Excel, Sheet per Table` behind a cover sheet, and `Excel, Single Sheet` with every section
stacked), both workbooks open with the report's title and the instant it was generated, and export
filenames are human (`Firm Usage 2026-08-31 19-48-43.xlsx` — the report's own name, the date, and
a readable time to the second, filesystem-unsafe characters dropped). Worksheet names are deduped
defensively so a title colliding with a section can never produce a workbook Excel refuses.

title: The capture waits for the page, streams its progress, and WHOIS finds the domain
entry:
**The capture waits for the page, shoots all of it, and narrates while it works — and a WHOIS
query for a hostname finds the domain's record.** The renderer was shooting a client-rendered page
mid-load (skeleton placeholders where content goes) and only the first viewport: the snapshot call
now passes `gotoOptions.waitUntil: networkidle2` with a timeout, a settle beat for lazy content,
and `screenshotOptions.fullPage`. A new streaming route (`POST /api/v1/safe-browse/stream`,
newline-delimited JSON stage lines) reports the redirect probe's settled facts while the renderer
still works, via a `CaptureStage` callback on `captureSafeView`; the page's loading viewport
narrates them ("Landed on youtube.com after 2 redirects. Rendering the page…") instead of a
generic line. And `lookupRegistration` walks a hostname up to the registrable domain that actually
answers — `www.youtube.com` is a registry 404 while `youtube.com` is the record the member meant —
stopping at the two-label floor and never walking an IP. Screen side: the tab strip aligns to the
address bar's height, the Different Site indicator (landed URL, badge, copy) lives only in the
Overview tab, the Soon marker survives only on the Live control's hover, and the WHOIS page
renders its result frame at rest.

title: A figure that is not a finite number never reaches a workbook cell
The deployment list leads with the pair that serves the app, and the copy glyph comes off
A count in a spreadsheet is a number: the Excel workbook joins the export menu
entry:
The export seam's third renderer: `$lib/export/render-xlsx.ts` writes a native Excel workbook —
one worksheet per section, a bold frozen header row, and typed number cells with the grouped
format wherever the document carries a figure. Built on write-excel-file, pinned exactly at 4.1.1
and imported lazily so no page carries it until someone exports; the adoption trail (exceljs,
SheetJS CE, and xlsx-populate weighed and declined) lives in the export seam's pending decision
record. Export document cells grew a second face for it: formatted text for the text and CSV
renderers, the raw number for Excel.

title: Retire the pillbox-updates stream note
The interface ships on its own Worker, and the panel stops warning about a state that is now normal
entry:
**The interface ships on its own Worker: the app's hostname is split by route pattern, and a UI
merge no longer has any reason to rebuild the API.**

The 2026-08-21 split design's two owner flags were answered and the cutover performed
(2026-08-31): the custom domain on `magna-carta` became route patterns on the zone —
`magna-carta-web` serves every path, `magna-carta` only `/api/*`, `/wopi/*`, `/search-objects/*`
and `/__dev/*`. Same origin, same cookie, no CORS; nothing auth-side moved. The decision, the one
deliberate departure from the design (the API Worker keeps its `assets` block as the local-dev
vehicle and one-gesture rollback — `wrangler dev` and the e2e suite serve the whole app from it),
and the accepted deploy-skew cost are recorded in the `the-interface-ships-on-its-own-worker` ADR.

In the repository, the change is mostly the record and one honest retirement: the version
overlay's page-versus-API "Different Builds" warning described a normal state once the two deploy
separately, so it is gone — the overlay's topology line explains why the rows may differ, and the
version poll's Update Available notice remains the one reload signal. The final decoupling lever
is dashboard state (dropping `apps/web/*` from the `magna-carta` project's Build Watch Paths) and
is tracked on the deploy queue.

title: The custody column reports, the export menu is one component, and the test pool wakes up
entry:
The Firm Usage By Location table's Custodian Items column now reports: a bounded recursive walk in
`@magna-carta/custodian` (`selectCustodyItemCountsByFirmLocationStatement`, covered by the
schema-name-sync fitness test) rolls held items up to the office their container-tree root binds
to, with external roots collected on a Held Offsite row and checked-out items counted nowhere. The
export seam gains `$lib/export/export-menu.svelte`, the one Download menu every exporting surface
uses (a format is one added entry), and the pending export decision now carries the .xlsx library
evaluation: exceljs rejected on unfixed advisories and inactivity, write-excel-file recommended.
Also fixed on this branch: the test pool deadlocked on the new lazy entrypoint's request-time
dynamic import, hanging every SELF.fetch test — the worker test setup now warms the module cache.

title: The viewer reads as one window, and the registration record comes to it
entry:
**The Safe Website Viewer composes as one window and leads with an Overview.** The shell and the
information tabs unify into one framed composition; clickable addresses (outbound links, redirect
hops — still buttons that capture in the viewer, never anchors to the suspect site) wear the
standard hyperlink register, now a standing rule in `docs/conventions/design-corrections.md`
alongside the unmistakable-toggle rule the Static/Live control is restyled to. The landed-URL row
gains its own copy control; the screenshot gains Download Image and a full-screen overlay; the
loading viewport shows the URL being captured, elapsed seconds, and one honest status line. A new
Overview tab leads the right side with facts derived from the capture already in hand (final
status, content type, server, redirect and link counts, captured-at, duration, the different-site
flag), and a Registration tab runs the WHOIS lookup in place for the captured host through the
shared lookup seam (lazy on first open, cached per host, with the same visible retry ladder) — no
redirect to the WHOIS page. Facts needing new backend probes (resolved IP, TLS certificate,
hosting provider) are recorded as seams, not faked.

title: The entrypoint stops spending the startup budget, and deploys pass validation again
entry:
**Production deploys stopped failing Worker validation: the app worker's entrypoint no longer
spends the startup budget.** Every deploy after the route count grew past a threshold failed with
error 10021 ("Script startup exceeded CPU time limit"), leaving `main` merged but undeployed. The
cost was the aggregate of the entrypoint's static import graph — every route module builds its zod
schemas and OpenAPI metadata at module scope. `src/index.ts` now keeps only the Durable Object
class re-exports (the one thing that must be synchronous at startup) and reaches the Hono app, the
Cron pass router, and the queue router through one dynamic import of the new
`src/event-dispatch.ts`, which the runtime evaluates on the first event instead of at validation:
roughly 1.5 s of local startup work became 0.24 s under `wrangler check startup`. The rule is
recorded in `docs/conventions/build-performance.md` (a Worker entrypoint keeps no static imports
beyond its Durable Object exports; measure entrypoint changes with `wrangler check startup`).

title: The version chip reports the whole fleet, and a running tab hears about a newer deploy
entry:
**The version chip reports the whole fleet, names every row by its deployed Worker, and tells you
when a newer deployment is live.**

The Build Versions panel's roster was eight workers short of the fleet and its rows carried invented
product names ("Malware Scan") beside, or instead of, the thing an operator would actually open.
Four changes, one panel:

- **Every magna-carta worker is listed.** The aggregate's roster is now the whole fleet — the edit,
  email, status and web workers join it — and a fitness test pins the roster to the wrangler configs
  on disk, so a worker added under `apps/` cannot silently stay off the overlay. The edit and status
  workers now mount the shared version route (and stamp their builds), the email worker gains a
  version-only `fetch` surface for the day it deploys, and the assets-only web worker answers
  through a static `/__version` file its build emits.
- **One name per line, and it is the real one.** Each deployment row is headed by the Cloudflare
  Worker it reports on, carried on the wire itself (`service` replaces `label` in
  `GET /api/v1/meta/versions`), with its state sentence beneath. The web app's own line stops
  borrowing the `magna-carta` name: the build the browser is running is its own line ("This page"),
  separate from the deployment list.
- **A newer deployment announces itself.** The app polls its own version (each build is named by
  its commit) and when a newer bundle is live the chip carries a warning dot and the panel leads
  with the notice and a Reload control. The page-versus-API skew check remains as the second
  detector.
- **Refresh means now.** The panel's Refresh and Retry pass `fresh=true`, which skips the server's
  brief cache and re-probes every worker — so the "checked N seconds ago" line starts over instead
  of climbing through a cache window.

title: An export is a document and a format is a renderer, and the usage report is stamped to the second
entry:
`$lib/export` — the common tabular export seam: one document shape (title, second-stamped instant,
table sections) built from exactly what a screen shows, with plain-text and CSV renderers over it
(byte-order mark, CRLF, RFC 4180 quoting). Firm Usage is the first consumer; its Download Report is
now a format menu, and its filenames carry a timestamp to the second. Native .xlsx waits on a
deliberate library adoption; Word and PDF belong to document assembly's one rendering path
(docs/decisions/pending/a-data-export-is-one-document-and-a-format-is-a-renderer.md).

title: Firm Usage sheds its bylines, gains a downloadable report, and the canvas contains its captions
entry:
The Firm Usage masthead byline and page footer are removed on the owner's direction (the tables are
the page), and a Download Report action renders the same response the tables drew as a dated
plain-text file (`$lib/tools/firm-usage/firm-usage-report.ts`, unit-tested). Also fixed at the
shell: the work canvas is now `position: relative`, so an absolutely positioned descendant (a
screen-reader-only table caption on any tall page) resolves against the canvas and clips with it,
instead of stretching the document into a second window scrollbar with bare background beneath the
shell.

title: The registry is retried visibly, and the viewer's address bar is the entry
entry:
**WHOIS retries registry faults itself, visibly, and the Safe Website Viewer becomes a real
browser shell.** The lookup seam gains `lookupWhoisWithRetries`: a transient upstream fault (the
502 the worker maps `RdapUpstreamFailure` to, or nothing answering) is retried up to three
attempts with short backoff, each attempt reported to the page, which shows "Trying again, attempt
2 of 3" in the loading card instead of stalling silently; the platform's own 429 is deliberately
never retried. Recorded as the standing rule "Retry a transient upstream fault yourself, visibly".
The viewer's result structure now renders at rest (the "result region is furniture" ruling): the
URL entry moves into the shell's own address bar as the one entry ("Load Website"), the landed URL
appears as a secondary row when a capture ends on a different site, back/forward/refresh navigate
a client-side capture history (`capture-history.ts`, unit-tested), outbound links load in the
viewer as new captures (buttons, never anchors), the URL is click-to-copy, tab panels are boxed
structures, and a Static/Live toggle renders with Live seamed behind the Soon affordance until the
interactive remote-browsing seam is built.

title: The four surfaces rebuilt to the settled rulings
entry:
The matter's Fees tab is a work-in-progress capture ledger, and the invoice window is where every operation on a bill lives.

Fees was built as a read-only projection of invoice lines: it listed what bills had already charged and called that the fee ledger. That put the effect where the cause belongs. A fee is a flat charge for professional services somebody records by hand — its own dated draft with a timekeeper, a description, an amount and a billing disposition — riding the same chain as a time entry and a cost, and claimed onto a draft invoice exactly as either of those is. It is never computed from time entries, drawn out of them, or consolidated from them. The ledger is now built on the shared work-in-progress surface: the columns are Date, Entry Number, Date Entered, Timekeeper, Description, Amount, Billable, Attachments and Status; the status column is the review chain rather than an invoice's standing; the `Drawn From` column and the vocabulary around it are gone; and a New Fee record window opens in the product's one two-pane window. The agreement is compacted to `Arrangement v3 · in force since <date>` with View and Amend, and the terms live behind View.

**No route serves a fee record yet**, so the ledger stands empty and says so, and every write renders where the design puts it, disabled, naming the store it waits on. That store — capture, update, void and delete over a fee row, plus the claim path — is the next slice of this work.

Billing gains the invoice window the design has asked for since round five. Identity, lines and totals sit on the left, or the claim workbench on a draft; Payments & Credits, History and Delivery are tabs beside them; and one action bar of fixed geometry sits beneath both, so an act a bill refuses is disabled with its reason rather than vanishing and moving everything else. Adjust Invoice takes its place on that bar, marked against the billing-model revision it waits on, rather than being left out. The sidebar is cut to identity, standing, a few figures, whether the bill was delivered, and Open Invoice; the money acts that were scattered across row menus now live in the window, where a reader can see what they are acting on. The register anchors on Created, and the `Total (all matters)` column and the rest of the multi-matter apparatus are gone.

A charge in the wrong ledger can be moved rather than voided and re-recorded. "Move to Another Ledger…" is in the shared row menu, and its dialog states what carries and what does not for the exact pair chosen — because the differences between the pairs are the whole decision — keeps the entry number, and explains why a moved record wears a number whose shape names where it was first written down. The move itself is one cross-table write with refusals a client cannot be trusted to enforce, and it is marked against that route.

**A status filter now offers every status the firm can hold, not only the ones present today.** A
filter whose choices come from the loaded rows tells a reader that "Closed" does not exist whenever
nothing is closed — which is a statement about this page of results dressed up as a statement about
the firm. The four columns whose values the firm itself declares — Status, Practice Area, Location and
Responsible Attorney — now seed the whole declared vocabulary in its own order, each with its true
count including zero. "Who is carrying nothing" is a real question and it was unanswerable before.
Client stays derived from rows, because nothing publishes a client directory.

**Opening a matter is one screen that grows instead of squeezing.** It fits its content first and caps
at the viewport second, and when it caps only the body moves — the header and the action bar hold, so
a refusal can never scroll out from under the hand reaching for it. Matter information and people sit
on the left across two tabs; the client and the conflict check stand together on the right, permanently
in view, because they are the same question.

Status replaces the old framing and reads Prospective, Active and Closed.

**Practice area is a dropdown that seeds itself.** The firm's own matter types existed as an API and
nothing ever seeded them, so a new firm met an empty field. Twenty starting areas are offered
alongside whatever the firm has already adopted; choosing one creates the firm's own type in that
moment, editable from then on, and hands it straight to the docket so the column and its filter know
about it at once.

**One correction could not land, and is rendered rather than dropped.** The create operation accepts
only Prospective or Active, so Closed stands in the list disabled, marked, naming exactly what it
waits on. Creating a matter already closed needs the contract widened.

The middle status is stored as `open` and printed as "Active" — a wire code is not a word anybody
reads. The two meet in one file and nowhere else.

**The Time Sheet opens from the top bar and belongs to the firm.** The owner's design puts it there —
it lives in the top bar and opens over whatever the person is doing, so capture never forces
navigation — and the port made it a per-matter modal reachable only from a matter's Time tab, removing
the Matter column and recording that removal as a design decision. It was not one.

One component now serves two doors: the Time Keeper chip opens it with no matter assumed, and a
matter's Time tab opens the same sheet pre-filtered to that matter. The chip was the last disabled
control in the shell saying it waited on a surface that had already arrived.

**A row without a matter is legal, because that is how time is actually captured** — somebody records
what they did before deciding where it belongs. Such a row holds typing, runs the timer, carries a
client-minted provisional code, counts in the incomplete tally, and never falls out of view when the
date scope moves. It is simply never sent: the capture route requires a matter, so the row states what
it still needs and writes itself the moment a matter is picked. No failed request, no error a person
has to interpret.

Two adjacent honesty calls came with it. A run started before a matter is chosen cannot become an
entry, so its seconds land on the row and the row writes itself through capture rather than through
the timer. And the permanent matter-scoped entry number the design mints cannot be minted here — no
route serves one — so a written row names that gap and says which provisional code it was held under.

Setting a matter on a row that is already an entry is refused out loud, because nothing moves an entry
between matters yet.

**The hard and soft cost distinction is gone from the cost surface.** The owner struck it in plain
words — it is not a real thing — and the ruling was recorded as settled: not renamed, not moved to
settings, not kept as a hidden field. It does not exist in the model, the capture form, the columns,
the filters, the review pane, or any copy.

It shipped anyway, because the surface was ported from a superseded draft rather than from the round
that struck it. Gone now: the class column and its filter, the class labels and their meanings, the
class field in the capture form, the class row in the details panel and the review window and the
print sheet, the class clause in the draft refusal, and the hard and soft figures in the panel
summary. Payee drops to three states, because the fourth existed only to carry the distinction, and
the largest-payee ranking now considers every cost that names somebody rather than only the hard
ones.

**The review gate reads off, matching the Time tab.** The two tabs of one matter disagreed about a
firm setting nothing serves: costs assumed review was on and showed Submit, Approve and Kick Back,
while time assumed off and showed none of it. A reader moving between them saw two different firms.
Off is the settled default, and off means the review vocabulary is absent rather than disabled. The
review window and its dialogs stay wired behind one flag, so serving the setting later is a single
change.

Column order, labels and figures come to the settled round: Description leads and is called
Description rather than Info, Recoverable is Billable, Receipt (one) is Attachments (many), and the
footer carries three figures — unbilled, billed, absorbed — rather than four.

Two stale affordances go with it. "Open in Billing" waited on a section that has shipped, and now
waits on the invoice reference it actually lacks. Unsubmit is rendered against a submitted cost,
marked, as the Time tab already does.

**One write still carries the struck field**, because the create contract makes it required: it is
supplied internally as a constant and no caller sees it. The field remains in the schema and, more
consequentially, in the finalize path, where it selects the ledger account — so removing it there is a
decision about accounting rather than a deletion.

title: The firm can see what it holds: the Firm Usage screen over a route that finally reads its own meters
entry:
**The Firm Usage screen ships at apps/web/src/routes/(app)/tools/firm-usage/** — the tables-only
quantitative snapshot over the extended `GET /api/v1/firm-usage`, computed on request, per
docs/decisions/pending/firm-usage-is-quantitative-tables-computed-on-request.md. Custodian holdings
render as a reserved column and per-firm compute as a Soon table, so both seams are visible on the
screen before their data exists.

`GET /api/v1/firm-usage` now composes the three AI meters that were written but read by no route
(`token_usage_meter`, `ai_search_usage_meter`, `ai_detection_usage`), plus new per-domain reads:
matters by type and by location (`@magna-carta/matters/queries`), the file versioning breakdown with
sizes (`@magna-carta/file-manager/usage`), location rows with staffing counts
(`@magna-carta/locations/statements`), Directory people/organization counts
(`@magna-carta/directory/usage`), and the active member count. Everything is computed on the
request — no cache, no snapshot — so a page nobody opens costs nothing. The roadmap's claim that the
token meter feeds the firm-usage surface, which had drifted ahead of the code, is now true.

title: A registry fault stops reading as an empty record, and the viewer gets its shell
entry:
**A registry fault no longer reads as an empty WHOIS record, and the Safe Website Viewer becomes a
shell-and-tabs surface.** `queryRdap` parsed every non-200 as an empty body, so a registry's
transient 429 rendered as "No registration record found" — which the next retry contradicted with
the real record. Only a 404 (RDAP's answer for an unregistered name) now parses as absence; every
other non-200, and a failed IANA bootstrap fetch, throws `RdapUpstreamFailure`, which the route
answers as a retryable 502 (`service-unavailable`) and the page renders as "the registry did not
answer, try again" — never an Error ID, never a false absence. IP-network records also gain their
`registrant` entity (the field the schema always declared and the parser never filled — 8.8.8.8
now names Google LLC). The viewer page is rebuilt per owner direction: a browser-shell viewport on
the left that holds its frame while the isolated browser works and populates only the finished
screenshot (nothing partial ever appears), with the capture's facts in tabs on the right
(Redirects, Page Text, Links, Headers). Both web-domains pages lose their intro paragraphs and
footers under the new "No info lines" ruling in `docs/conventions/design-corrections.md`.

title: Retire the safe-website-viewer stream note
Open an untrusted website at arm's length, from a screen this time
entry: **Safe Website Viewer tool page.** The `web-domains` pair is complete on the screen side: a new page at `/tools/safe-website-viewer` over the existing chokepoint route (`POST /api/v1/safe-browse`), with the branching in a DOM-free seam (`apps/web/src/lib/tools/safe-browse/safe-browse.ts`) on the WHOIS page's same-origin-fetch pattern. Everything the page renders is inert: the screenshot is an `` from base64, extracted text stays escaped text, and the suspect page's outbound links render as plain text, never anchors. The catalog entry advances `soon` to `alpha`, so the listing tile, list row, and command palette entry become launchable; palette synonyms ("phishing", "redirect") widen its search net. A 502 from the remote renderer reads as a transient outage to retry, not a fault to quote — the render engine is Cloudflare Browser Rendering, an account entitlement still queued in `docs/deploy-queue.md`, so captures answer that outage state until it is enabled. Three owner rulings issued against the WHOIS page in review land with it (recorded in `docs/conventions/design-corrections.md`): the query control sits at the reading edge rather than the masthead's far-right actions slot, intro copy is one flowing paragraph, and orienting text persists through result states.

title: The financial surfaces, the directory, and the write path that could never have worked
entry:
**Both Worker configs said the application's hostname was unattached; it has been attached and serving all along.** `apps/api-worker/wrangler.jsonc` described its `workers.dev` URL as "the current public URL until magnacarta.esq attaches", and `apps/web-worker/wrangler.jsonc` said the single-page-application split was blocked because the cutover "needs a zone hostname the account does not have yet". A read of `GET /accounts/{account_id}/workers/domains/records` shows the apex bound to the `magna-carta` Worker as a custom domain, enabled, with `status.magnacarta.esq` beside it.

**The inference that produced it is the part worth keeping.** A custom domain is account state: it is attached in the dashboard, appears in no `wrangler.jsonc`, and `wrangler deploy` does not remove it. So a Worker carrying `workers_dev: true` with no `routes` block can be answering a real apex hostname, and "no routes in the config, therefore workers.dev only" is a conclusion the config cannot support. Both comments now say so, and point at the read rather than restating today's answer — the rule `docs/conventions/operations.md` opens with, after this repository disagreed with the live configuration four times.

The web Worker's blocker is restated rather than removed, because the split really is still blocked — for the other reason. A custom domain consumes the whole hostname, so the apex has to be converted to route patterns on the zone before two Workers can split it by path and before `magna-carta-web` can serve anyone. That is a mechanism, so it does not rot. The standing invariant survives unchanged: the app Worker's `assets` block stays until a live routing read shows the interface reaching users another way.

Comments only — no `run_worker_first`, `assets`, binding, var or trigger value changed.

**A firm can now record a client's telephone number.** It could not before. `directory_phone` and
`directory_address` were real tables with no domain module at all — not one statement in the
repository inserted a phone number or an address — and email had a write path reachable only from
inbound mail capture. All three are reachable now, through fourteen operations under the firm-scoped
chokepoint, with a combined read that answers all three channels at once.

**Permission and preference are separate facts.** A contact point records whether it may be used and
whether it is preferred, because someone can be reachable by a method that is not their preference.
At most one point is preferred across all three channels, since "write to me" is one answer about
every channel rather than one answer per channel. Withdrawing permission is what the surface offers
instead of deletion — deleting the value loses the instruction that came with it.

**A date of birth is a date again.** It was filed as an encrypted identifier, which is matched only by
exact blind index, and a date of birth carries too few plausible values to index safely — so the code
deliberately refused, and the date could not be searched or range-queried. It is now a plain date on
the person, with date of death and a separate deceased flag beside it, registered in the PII registry.
The birth-year compromise was withdrawn on the way: a year cannot fill in a court form.

**Addresses take the international field set** — no hardcoded state or ZIP, no required field — and the
seam a validation provider would land in ships without the provider. Sending a client's address to a
third party is a disclosure only the firm can authorise, so the recommendation is recorded and nothing
is adopted.

**The three contact tables are reachable.** `directory_email`, `directory_phone` and
`directory_address` had been in the per-firm schema since the baseline migration with nothing able to
write to them: phone and address had no domain module at all, and `contact-email.ts` was a write path
built for and reachable only from inbound mail capture. Twenty-five directory routes touched none of
the three, and `entity-sections.ts` listed seven panes, none of them Contact. A firm could not record a
client's telephone number.

This change adds `contact-phone.ts`, `contact-address.ts`, `contact-points.ts`, `contact-preference.ts`,
`phone-number.ts` and `postal-address.ts` to `packages/directory`, lifts `contact-email.ts` to a general
write path, mounts thirteen routes on `apps/api-worker/src/routes/directory.ts`, and adds the Contact
and Dates panes to the record screen. One additive migration
(`20260830T120000_directory-contact-points.sql`) carries every column: the plan had been to reach the
tables first and add columns after, and that was reversed deliberately, because each of the owner's
rulings on this pass is a column the ENTRY SURFACE has to be able to take and building the pane twice
was the alternative.

The columns: `contact_permitted` / `contact_preferred` / `contact_note` on all three tables, with at
most one preferred contact point per entity ACROSS the three (three UPDATEs in the write batch, since
"write to me" is one answer about every channel and `is_primary` is a different fact — the channel's
default row); `contact_system` / `contact_use` / `country_calling_code` / `national_number` /
`extension` / `country_region_code` on phone, with `number` keeping its meaning as the number AS
ENTERED; the international address field set (`recipient`, `organization_name`, `street_two`,
`dependent_locality`, `sorting_code`) plus `address_use`, `address_type` and a `normalized_key` that is
a duplicate key and deliberately not a canonical postal form; the four verification columns on all
three; and `date_of_birth` / `date_of_death` / `deceased` on `directory_person`, in the clear and
registered for erasure. `structurePhoneNumber` implements the E.164 assignment rule rather than
carrying a metadata library, so a national-form number yields a null calling code rather than a guessed
one.

Eight of the design's open questions were answered by the owner and every section they touched was
rewritten in
[`docs/specs/2026-08-30-directory-entity-model-design.md`](docs/specs/2026-08-30-directory-entity-model-design.md):
the date of birth is the full date in plaintext (the `birth_year` compromise is withdrawn), citizenship
is dropped, the organization taxonomy is deferred whole, a failed verification never gates a send, and
the point person on an organization is an edge type rather than a flag because the point person is
frequently not an employee. Three decision fragments are new — the permission-and-preference split, the
point-of-contact edge, and the address-provider recommendation — and four existing ones were amended to
what was built. `point_of_contact_for` is decided and NOT built: a new `EDGE_TYPES` value must be
classed in `packages/conflicts/src/edge-classes.ts` in the same change, which was outside this stream's
file ownership.

**A record is now edited in the window that reads it, and the window stops growing before its tabs
do.** Three owner rulings landed in the record window at once.

Editing happens in place. `onEdit` is gone from the shell, so there is no callback a consumer could
hang a second surface off; the header's Edit control raises the shell's own `editing` state, and the
record snippet is handed the mode so one snippet renders values or fields. The tabs are deliberately
not told the mode, which is what makes "the context pane stays read-only in both modes" true by
construction rather than by five record types each remembering it. Edit refuses entry twice over: a
consumer's own reason, and the absence of a commit path, because a mode with no way to save is worse
than no mode. Commit and abandon are the shell's, always the last two controls in that order — a
person aims at the commit without reading it, and a bar whose terminal control is worded differently
per record type costs exactly that.

A record that fits does not scroll. The panel sizes to its content, so a short record opens as a
short window with no scrollbar and no empty band under the last field; only a record that genuinely
cannot fit caps at the viewport, and then the body alone moves. The header and the action bar never
scroll away. The two statements read as contradictory and had been re-litigated more than once, so
they are written into the recipe as one ordered preference with the order stated.

Growth goes to the tabs, not to the record. The left pane stops at a measure wide enough for a
three-column field row and narrow enough that a description is not set across a monitor; everything
past it goes to attachments and history, which are the half that reads better wide. It is a bound
rather than a ratio, which is why the two panes are flex items: a track ratio cannot say "this one
stops and that one carries on".

**And the width token governed nothing until it was measured.** The recipe declared
`max-inline-size: var(--mc-size-record-window)` on a panel that arrives wearing the dialog's own
`max-w-lg`, and a Tailwind utility outranks the components layer whatever the selector — so the
window opened at 512px while its recipe named 1024. The cap is now a utility fed by the same token
(`--container-record-window`, registered in `mergeClasses` so two `max-w-*` classes cannot both
survive the merge), and the recipe says why it is not declared there. The trap is general: any
recipe setting a width on an element that also carries a width utility loses silently, and nothing
scans for it.

`ScreenSearch` — the product's one control for searching within a screen, distinct from the top bar's command palette.

Eleven list surfaces answered "search this screen" four different ways, sharing no code: matters and the file manager each hand-rolled an expand-from-icon search, the directory and custodian carried an always-present labelled field, the Time Sheet had the shape specified but only in a mockup, and matter parties, matter costs, notifications, user administration and tools had nothing at all. The design system's own `DataTable.Search` was built for the job and had zero consumers — because it bound straight to a table's global filter and so could only narrow rows already in the browser, which is exactly why the screens that search on a server went and built their own.

The component carries the shape the standing list-screen rule already decided. It rests as an icon, so a screen nobody is searching pays no vertical space for it; it expands on use and collapses when left empty; a live query keeps it open behind a single accent hairline, so a narrowed list carries its reason on screen. There is no clear button — Escape clears the query, a second Escape closes the control and hands focus back to the icon that opened it.

It is one component by construction: registered in the one-implementation registry, so a second file claiming the name fails the gate. And it serves either transport without the calling screen writing anything different — the screen hands over `onsearch` and says whether to run it on every keystroke, for data already here, or after a pause in typing, for a request that leaves the machine. The control owns the query, the debounce and the in-flight flag; it owns no results. `DataTable.Search` is now a thin preset over it that supplies `onsearch` from a table, so the common case stays one line.

Three things ship as seams, built and exercised in the catalog but wired to no screen: a scope control at the field's leading edge, an in-field match count, and a shortcut key. Each says in the code what will use it. The scope names the surface it searches and will never offer "everywhere" — searching everything is the top bar's job.

Adopting it on the screens is separate work, and one of those adoptions removes a defect: in a right-aligned action row the search has to sit to the leading side of the primary action, or the primary action slides sideways on the first keystroke.

**Uploading a document from the file manager filed it at the matter root, whichever folder the
reader was standing in.** The screen shows one folder at a time, so the file simply was not there
afterwards — indistinguishable from an upload that failed.

`POST /api/v1/uploads` has always accepted `folderId` and `documentTypeId`. The document loop's client
type does not declare either, so neither was ever sent. Two smaller contributors sat on top of it:
the upload never asked where the file should go, and the surface never navigated to the destination
once the file landed.

The file manager now runs its own destination-aware reservation, reusing the shared put, complete and
status calls and re-declaring only the reservation itself, sending `null` explicitly rather than
omitting a field. **The test asserts the reservation body rather than that the ceremony completed** —
a test of the second kind would have passed for the entire life of the defect.

Alongside it, the file manager is ported from the owner's own surface: one table carrying the same
column machinery as every other ledger, a computed right-click model rather than a template of
conditions, a five-tab details panel whose hashes genuinely recompute against the integrity endpoint,
and the folder rail finally wired to the tree component that was built for it and never connected.

**The matter's Billing tab carries the bill register and the fee ledger**, both ported from the
owner's own surfaces and both composed on the product's one grid — so sorting, in-header filters,
show and hide, reorder, pin, resize, selection, the totals row and the counts strip are inherited
rather than decided again.

Wired to the billing API that already existed: creating an invoice, claiming unbilled work, editing a
line, voiding a draft, finalizing, credit notes, write-offs, applying a client credit, recording
delivery, and reading invoices, credit notes, deliveries and client credits alongside the matter's
unbilled total and its fee arrangement.

**Money is integer minor units end to end, and the only division by one hundred is at the render
boundary.** Typed amounts are parsed digit by digit rather than through a float, because
`parseFloat("1.15") * 100` is `114.99999999999999` — pinned by a test.

Seven gaps between the design and what can be served are named on the screen rather than papered
over. There is no per-matter invoice listing, so the register is client-wide with This Matter as its
leading money column and the all-matters total beside it — which is the mockup's own distinction, now
load-bearing. Nothing serves a trust-account listing, so applying trust funds ships as the full
designed dialog with the act disabled and its dependency named, and the unreachable client call was
removed rather than shipped. Claiming works and releasing a claim does not. The matter read carries
no client, so the client is resolved from the party wearing that role, and a matter without one
refuses to draft a bill and says why.

**The matter's Costs tab is the ledger that was designed for it**, ported from the owner's own
surface rather than approximated from a description of it. What stood there was a read-only
six-column table; what was designed is a working ledger, and the difference was never a smaller
version of the same thing.

Eleven columns with the grid's own sorting, filtering, hiding, reordering, pinning, resizing,
selection and totals. A four-figure footer — advanced, recoverable, billed, absorbed. A details panel
with three faces: the matter's own summary with its largest payees, a single cost with its standing,
its chain and its memo, and a multi-selection that counts what can be submitted or approved and
excludes voids from the amount it names. Recording and editing a cost, with the sentence that says
what the class and billing choice will mean. The review queue walker, kick-back, void, the print
sheet, and a problem report that reaches the real incidents endpoint.

It is wired to the costs API that already existed rather than to fixtures: listing, create, patch,
submit, approve, kick back and void, with the directory search behind the payee picker and the
expense-code catalogue behind the code labels.

**Where the screen cannot show something, it says which fact is missing rather than rendering an
empty cell.** The listing projection drops five columns the table already knows how to draw —
`receipt_file_id`, `kick_back_reason`, `invoice_id`, `created_at`, `created_by` — so entry number,
date entered, entered by, receipt, the kicked-back reason, and the invoice a billed cost rides are
each marked as not served. That is one projection change with no migration behind it, and it is the
single largest gap between this screen and the design it came from.

**The Directory has a listing.** It never had one: the screen was designed to be searched and not browsed, so `MINIMUM_QUERY_LENGTH` characters had to be typed before anything appeared, and a firm that had entered twenty clients opened it to an instruction. The reasoning was half right — a ranked, capped answer must never be dressed as an index — and drew the wrong conclusion; the answer is to build the index.

`GET /api/v1/directory/entities` is the new read: both node tables unioned into one sequence, ordered by a name key computed per table so a row never sorts under one name and prints another, cursor-paged over `(sort name, id)` through the existing opaque token, and carrying `total` for the whole record rather than the page. `kind` narrows it. Deleted and merged-away records are excluded. It lives in `packages/directory/src/entity-listing.ts` and reaches the firm database through the chokepoint like every other directory read. The ordering key is computed rather than stored, so the read scans the node tables; a stored normalized sort column is the change if that ever stops being cheap enough.

The screen now shows the index at rest and the search answer only when a query is asked, as two visibly different objects: the index is the platform's one table (sortable, filterable, paged, counted), and the search answer keeps the firm's relevance order, is never re-sorted client-side, and keeps its capped line.

**A firm using this platform cannot record a client's telephone number, and nothing in the schema
says so.** `directory_email`, `directory_phone` and `directory_address` have been in the per-firm
schema since the baseline migration. They are temporal, soft-deleted, indexed, carry an `is_primary`
flag whose enforcement the schema comments describe, and all three are registered for subject
erasure. Twenty-five directory routes, and not one touches any of them. The email table has a write
path built for inbound capture and reachable only from it; phone and address have no domain module
at all, so there is not one statement anywhere in the repository that inserts a telephone number or
an address for a person. The record screen lists seven panes and none of them is Contact.

The design pass that found it is at
[`docs/specs/2026-08-30-directory-entity-model-design.md`](docs/specs/2026-08-30-directory-entity-model-design.md),
and its first conclusion is that the model is much deeper than the screen suggests, so this is a
completion rather than a rebuild. Names are already temporal, role-typed, phonetically coded and
match-keyed twice over; identifiers are already one sealed row per value with a per-type frozen
normalize transform and an explicit, reasoned blind-index policy. Neither is touched.

What the pass proposes, grounded in RFC 6350, FHIR R4, NIEM's `nc:PersonType`, schema.org, Popolo,
and the professional-conduct rules the data exists to serve: the contact tables reached by an API
and a pane before anything structural changes; a phone split into what technology answers it and in
what context, with a canonical E.164 form beside the number as entered and the extension in its own
column, because fax is a technology and work is a context and one free-text label cannot be both;
identifier types promoted from bare strings to registered scheme descriptors shipped as package
reference data, with the issuing jurisdiction moved out of the sealed value into its own column and
the frozen transform still seeing byte-identical input so no existing blind index is invalidated;
date of birth, date of death and a deceased flag moved onto the person, because a range query over
ciphertext is not a query and `IdentifierNotIndexableError` already exists as the symptom; an
organization given a kind, a jurisdiction of formation and a life, which the schema's own
`court_entity_id` and `estate_entity_id` have needed since they were written; provenance and a
verification status on every contact point and identifier, where `failed` — returned mail, a bounce,
a disconnected line — is the state with nowhere to live today and the one an affidavit of diligence
turns on; a no-contact warning derived per matter from who represents the party rather than stored as
a flag on a person, because Rule 4.2 is scoped to the matter and a stale warning teaches people to
dismiss warnings; and the edge catalog split so a constituent who can bind an organization is
distinguishable from one who cannot, since the conflicts traversal currently spends its control
budget on a mailroom clerk with the same weight it spends on a chief executive.

Nine decision fragments accompany it. Eight open questions are put to the owner rather than settled,
the largest being whether a date of birth sits in plaintext, in plaintext as a birth year beside the
retained sealed date, or unchanged.

**The matters docket shows every matter by default and the scope control is gone.** "The working
docket / Open matters / Closed matters / Consultations" duplicated a narrowing the table's own Status
filter already performs, and the owner ruled it out twice.

Removing it needed a read change rather than a deletion: the matters listing omits unnumbered
consultations by default and its status parameter takes one status, never all. So the screen now
reads both streams in parallel, merges them, and carries the two server cursors as one token. Merging
across page boundaries is safe only because the grid sorts what it holds, and that reason is written
where the merge happens — it would not be safe for a surface rendering rows in fetch order. Either
stream failing fails the whole read, because half a docket looks exactly like a small firm.

**Opening a matter is one screen.** Entry on the left across three tabs — the matter, the client, the
people — and Clearance standing permanently on the right: the conflict check with its subjects
derived live from the title and client as they are typed, the consultation fee, and the trust
deposit. Clearance is deliberately not a fourth tab, and the reason is recorded: it is not more data
being entered, it is the gate the entry has to pass, and a gate behind a tab is one somebody has to
remember to go and look at. It fits 1280x720 without scrolling.

**A defect on the screen whose job is saying who carries the matter:** the Responsible Attorney field
showed its ghost text while the seat was filled. It now shows who holds the seat at rest and clears
to the whole roster on focus, and a collecting seat empties after each pick.

The matter's Custodian tab stops reading Soon — the surface is real and the sidebar already said
Alpha. Every other section was audited against its route in the same pass; the ones still marked Soon
are stubs, correctly.

The operations runbook and the owner action queue no longer record any current value of Cloudflare account state — connected Workers, production branches, root directories, build commands, Build Watch Paths, build caching, hostnames and routes, deploy dates, build outcomes. Each is replaced by the runnable command that returns it.

The reason is a count. `operations.md` wrote those values down and disagreed with the live configuration four separate times: a connected-Worker roster short by five; the edit Worker's root directory, deploy command and branch, all three true when written and all three false when next read; two Build Watch Paths matching no file, which suppresses rebuilds silently rather than failing; and a conclusion drawn from `apps/api-worker/wrangler.jsonc` that no custom domain was attached to the app Worker, when the account has an active zone bound to it as one. Each was corrected. Each correction decayed the moment somebody used the dashboard, which leaves no commit behind.

A drift-detecting check was considered and rejected: it needs a committed copy of the truth to diff against, which is the same snapshot in a format that compares, and it cannot run in the gate of record because that gate has no Cloudflare credentials and must not require network.

What stays is what no API returns — the decisions and why, the operator procedures, the failure modes that have each cost a deploy, and the invariants. `operations.md` now opens with the rule and the four drifts as its evidence, so the next person tempted to paste today's values back in reads the reason first.

Falsified along the way, and corrected: the fleet-wide production-branch reconciliation and the missing `packages/build-identity/*` watch paths were both carried as open owner items and are not; `magna-carta` is reachable at a custom domain, not only at `workers.dev`; and it does have Build Watch Paths rather than rebuilding on every push.

**The Time Sheet is ported from the owner's own surface**, which is an editable grid rather than a
table that opens a window. That distinction is the whole of it: what stood on the matter's Time tab
was a read-only ledger and a record window, and neither is a smaller version of a sheet somebody
captures a day's work in.

Rows edit in place and autosave on leaving a cell, and the leading state mark says which of saving,
saved, saved-but-incomplete, not-yet-written or failed the row is in. Undo and redo carry forty
bounded steps with split menus naming what each step was, and an undo writes the restored values
back rather than only redrawing them. Scope is Today, Yesterday or This week against the firm's own
first weekday, with a custom range that applies as it is picked — and a row just added or re-dated is
never dropped out of view. Search expands from its icon and collapses when left empty; clear-filters
exists only while a filter is in play.

**The timer is the firm's real one, not a local stopwatch.** The single-active-timer routes already
existed, so starting a second row says the first was stopped and kept its time; a row that is already
an entry takes the elapsed time onto its own duration, and a row that is not becomes the entry the
timer commits.

Nothing was simplified because an endpoint is missing. Time Code, Date Entered, Rate, Files and
Entered By render as real columns naming what they wait on, and the capture route requires a positive
duration and a narrative — so a fresh row lives on the sheet holding what is typed into it, marked
not yet written with the reason, and writes itself the moment it is acceptable.

**Two consumer defects were found by measuring rather than reading.** The record pane's field rows
broke on a viewport media query when the pane's width is a property of the window, which is exactly
what collided three labels into one unreadable run. And a Soon badge overflowed the pane by thirty
pixels in a pane that does not scroll sideways, so it was simply cut off. Both are container-width
problems and are now solved with the width the pane actually controls.

**Every write on the Time surface except creating an entry was answered `400` before the handler
ran.** The contract declares `Idempotency-Key` required on update, submit, approve, kick-back and
void; the client sent one only on create, and the transport adds the header solely when a caller
supplies it.

So a row typed into the Time Sheet saved once, and every keystroke after that settled into "Not
saved. The server answered 400." Striking a row failed the same way. Saving from the record window
failed the same way. The autosave was architecturally present and could not succeed.

**No test could have caught it.** Nothing anywhere in the web application asserted what a surface put
on the wire — method, path, headers or body — so the whole suite passed with this live. The key is
now a required parameter of every write, making an omission a type error at the call site rather than
a failed save, and the new test asserts the header on all six writes from a table that a new write
cannot be added to without carrying it. The defect was reintroduced deliberately to confirm the test
fails: seven failures across two files.

Seven further defects went with it. "New Entry" created two rows and left one permanently phantom.
Undo announced "Undid striking this entry" when nothing un-strikes one, because no unvoid route
exists — it now refuses the step and says so at the moment it happens. Submit and approve discarded
their outcomes, so a refusal was silent. Two capabilities the code claimed were "rendered disabled
with the dependency named" were not rendered at all. The footer and the Worked column disagreed while
a timer ran. Duplicate opened a blank draft. And the forty-step undo bound had no test — changing it
to four, or to infinity, broke nothing.

title: The owner's design surfaces come into the repository, and five screens get built from them
entry:
**The version overlay now explains each non-answer instead of leaving a two-word badge to be read
as an outage.** "Not deployed", "Unreachable" and "Not reporting" are three different facts about a
deployment, and a bare badge separated none of them: a service this deployment was never wired to
looked identical to a service that failed the read, which looked identical to a healthy service
whose build simply predates the version route. Each row now carries the sentence that says which
one it is, on the line the reported rows use for their timestamps.

Two smaller repairs ride along. The build-identity stamp reads the build runner's own commit
variable (`WORKERS_CI_COMMIT_SHA`, `GITHUB_SHA`) when git cannot answer for the checkout, so a
Worker built on a runner without a usable `.git` reports the commit it was built from rather than
`dev`; a commit that no source can name still reports `dev`, unchanged. And the web-versus-API skew
call compares commits by prefix rather than by equality, because the two sides abbreviate the hash
independently and an equality test would raise "Different Builds" over a deployment that is in step.

title: The record family, the firm's roster, and sign-in working off production again
entry:
**The matters list now names the responsible attorney**, and every screen that has to put a name to a colleague can.

`GET /api/v1/members` answers the firm's roster — display name, whether the member is still here, the roles they hold, and whether a professional profile has been written. No email address, no direct dial, no permission set: it answers who is on the firm, not how to reach them or what they may do. It rides its own capability, `firm:readMembers`, seeded to every default role including Read-only — adding a person to the firm is Owner/Admin's, and knowing who is already in it is not the same act. The read is un-paged, because a roster is bounded by the firm's headcount rather than by its activity, and a listing joining names against it has to have the whole lookup before any row renders honestly.

The docket's new **Responsible Attorney** column resolves that identifier the way Practice Area and Location already do — one roster read per screen, never a request per row. A matter whose responsible member the roster cannot name reads empty rather than printing a `user_…` handle, and a colleague who has left is still named on the matters they carried. The column had been left off the list entirely, with a note on the page saying why; the note is gone.

Two repairs travelled with it, both of the same kind — an account nobody can sign into:

- **Signing in worked only from the production origin.** Declaring the deployment's public URL had, as a side effect, made it the only origin the sign-in endpoint would accept a request from — so `wrangler dev` on localhost, a preview deployment, and every test that signs in were refused with "Invalid origin". The origin a request actually arrived at is trusted again, alongside the configured one; a genuine cross-site request still carries somebody else's origin and is still refused.
- **The development seed left a passwordless account.** Re-seeding against warm local state found the existing user and skipped its credential, then printed a password that did not work. The seed now converges every field it promises — firm attachment, verification, and the credential — so a re-seed repairs an unsignable account instead of reporting success for one.

The platform's one table now obeys the rulings it was built to carry, and it can group and mark its rows.

Four settled rulings were already contradicted by the table that shipped days ago, all of them in the per-column filter. The set filter's narrow field said "Type to narrow the choices" and the text filter said "Contains…" — both struck, because every ghost text is the FIELD'S NAME and never a description of what to do; each now carries the column's own label. The set filter's select-all was a static checkbox that stated what IS; it is now one control that states what pressing it will DO, reading "Select none" while everything is on and "Select all" the moment anything is off. And the set filter carried a "Clear This Filter" button, which said the same thing that control already says: a set filter with everything selected IS no filter, so it now carries no clear control at all. The other filter kinds keep theirs, and still only while a filter is in play.

A fifth was in the columns menu: an unpinned column's control drew the crossed-out pin, a different glyph for what is meant to be one glyph in two states. There is one pin everywhere the pin state shows — pinned rows and pinned columns alike — and fill is the only difference.

Alongside the conformance work the table gained the two things every list says about a row before it says anything about the row's data. **Row groups:** pinned items sit above everything, separated by a rule, in the order the member arranged them rather than the table's sort — a pinned file leads a list whose folders would otherwise sort ahead of it. A pinned key whose row a filter excluded contributes nothing, so the footer's "n of m" stays true. **Row marks:** one vocabulary — the filled pin on the row's first cell, a dashed edge while a row waits on a cut or a copy (a cut row speaks quieter, because it is leaving), and that same quieter voice for a row present but not of the list's own kind, which is what a deleted match among live search results and an event inherited from a folder act both need.

Every fixed ruling is pinned by a test that asserts the property the ruling names, so the next round finds them asserted rather than remembered. The developer console's table-states gallery gains the groups-and-marks specimen.

title: Real mail, now that a failed send says so
A password is chosen where the account is, the matters list works, and the runbooks catch up
entry:
**A password is chosen at registration, and the credential is committed with the account.** Every joining path — `registrations.confirm`, the firm-provision consumer's owner adoption, `members.invite`, invitation redemption — created a `user` row with no credential `account` row, on the theory that the mailed password-reset link would bring one into being. It does: Better Auth's reset endpoint inserts a credential account when `findAccounts` turns up none (verified against the installed 1.6.22, `api/routes/password.mjs`). But it only does so if the mail arrives and somebody acts on it, so a deployment with no `EMAIL_FROM` — which resolves the logging adapter and delivers nothing — produced accounts nobody could ever sign in to. The only symptom was the library logging `Credential account not found` from `api/routes/sign-in.mjs`.

`StartRegistrationRequest` now carries `password` (optional at the schema layer, bounded by Better Auth's own configured 8–128; required by the two doors that create something, refused as a field-level 422 naming the rule). It is hashed in that request with the library's own hasher and stored on `registration.credential_hash` — a new nullable column, so a registration in flight across the deploy still completes the account-less way it started. Confirming inserts the `user` row, its credential `account` row and the verified-email flag in ONE batch; the founding door passes the same verifier through `provisionFirm`, which commits it with the owner. `ConfirmRegistrationResponse` gains `next: signIn | checkEmail`. `joining-credentials.ts` is the one home for the hash and the account statement.

Redemption deliberately still mails its link: the code, surname and date of birth prove no mailbox, and that link is the only thing standing between somebody who guessed all three and another person's account.

**And an unguarded send no longer escapes as a 500.** `registrations.start` answers a retryable `503` (`mail-undeliverable`, Error ID, retry window) and keeps the row it committed — both branches identically, so a mail outage cannot become the account-existence oracle the endpoint is built to deny. The reset-based paths could not be guarded at the call site at all: Better Auth's `runInBackgroundOrAwait` awaits the send and swallows what it throws into its own logger, so `api.requestPasswordReset` resolves whether or not a mail left. The guard therefore sits on the PORT `app.ts` hands the library, where the failure is counted (`email.delivery_failed`, dimensions `surface` + `messageClass`) and correlated. No send path anywhere logs a body. `createAuth` also reads `baseURL` from `APP_BASE_URL` when set, silencing the library's cold-start warning.

**The matters list is a real docket, and a matter can be opened from it.** The screen was a hardcoded
empty state with a permanently disabled "New matter" button — no query, no rows, and a `disabled`
attribute written into the markup rather than derived from anything. The backend it was standing in
front of had been complete for months: create, cursor-paginated list, get, patch, and the whole
open/close/reopen/renumber lifecycle. Nothing was missing except the screen.

It now reads the firm's own matters through the listing and renders them on `DataTable.Grid`, the
platform's one table, so the docket inherits the settled machinery rather than reimplementing it:
type-aware sorting, the one-mechanism per-column filters, column show/hide, drag-reorder, pinning,
resize, and the counts footer. Columns are matter number, title, client, status, practice area,
Location (hidden until a firm asks for it) and created date. A scope control selects what the
listing is asked for, and the search box runs the server's own search over title, number and client
rather than narrowing the rows already on screen.

**"New matter" opens a real matter.** The dialog carries the contract's required set and nothing
invented: a title, whether the file starts as an opened matter or an unnumbered consultation, the
client, and the firm's own practice-area and Location vocabularies. The number is deliberately not a
field — it is drawn by the firm's counter at the moment the matter opens, atomically, and a field
for it would be a field for breaking that. Every submit carries an idempotency key, so a retry
cannot open a second matter.

Three gaps are on the screen rather than hidden, because a docket that quietly cannot answer a
question is worse than one that says so:

- **The responsible attorney is not a column.** The listing answers an identifier for it and nothing
  on the server publishes the firm's members, so naming them would cost one request per row and
  printing the handle would be printing a handle at a person. The dialog's own responsible-attorney
  field renders for real, showing the person creating the matter, disabled and marked "Soon" with
  the dependency named.
- **The date column says "Created", not "Opened".** The listing serves the creation instant; a
  matter opened months after the consultation that started it has two dates and only the detail read
  carries the second.
- **Sorting and the column filters cover what has been loaded.** The listing is cursor-paged, so the
  footer counts the page rather than the firm until the record is fully read, and the line under
  "Load more" says exactly that.

A refused open now says where to fix it: opening a numbered matter needs the firm's numbering
scheme, and the refusal points at the settings page that configures one instead of leaving the
server's one-line reason to be interpreted.

The matter status register — prospective, open, closed, with their labels and their subtle badge
tones — moved out of the matter header into one shared module both surfaces read, so the header's
seal and the docket's status column cannot drift apart. Closed stays quiet neutral: a closed matter
is archived-but-additive, not a failure.

title: Account-first joining, seven rounds of design rulings, and the plan that ports them
entry:
